title: Relationship to Local Security Policy and Other Policies
shall_text: The local agency may complement the CJIS Security Policy with a local policy, or the agency may develop their own stand-alone security policy; however, the CJIS Security Policy shall always be the minimum standard and local policy may augment, or increase the standards,… ...and local policy may augment, or increase the standards, but shall not detract from the CJIS Security Policy standards.

title: Relationship to Local Security Policy and Other Policies
shall_text: The agency shall develop, disseminate, and maintain formal, documented procedures to facilitate the implementation of the CJIS Security Policy and, where applicable, the local security policy.

title: Relationship to Local Security Policy and Other Policies
shall_text: The policies and procedures shall be consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance.

title: CJIS Systems Agencies (CSA)
shall_text: The head of each CSA shall appoint a CJIS Systems Officer (CSO).

title: CJIS Systems Agencies (CSA)
shall_text: Such decisions shall be documented and kept current.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: Pursuant to The Bylaws for the CJIS Advisory Policy Board and Working Groups, the role of CSO shall not be outsourced.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: The CSO shall set, maintain, and enforce the following:

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: 1. Standards for the selection, supervision, and separation of personnel who have access to CJI.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: 2. Policy governing the operation of computers, access devices, circuits, hubs, routers, firewalls, and other components that comprise and support a telecommunications network and related CJIS systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI, guaranteeing the priority, confidentiality, integrity, and availability of service needed by the criminal justice community.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: a. Ensure appropriate use, enforce system discipline, and ensure CJIS Division operating procedures are followed by all users of the respective services and information.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: b. Ensure state/federal agency compliance with policies approved by the APB and adopted by the FBI.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: c. Ensure the appointment of the CSA ISO and determine the extent of authority to the CSA ISO.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: d. Ensure the designation of a Terminal Agency Coordinator (TAC) within each agency with device access to CJIS systems.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: e. Ensure each agency having access to CJI has someone designated as the Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: f. Ensure the Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities receives enhanced security awareness training (ref. Awareness and Training (AT)).

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: g. Approve access to FBI CJIS systems.

title: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO)
shall_text: h. Assume ultimate responsibility for managing the security of CJIS systems within their state and/or agency.

title: Contracting Agency (CA)
shall_text: A CA is an agency, whether a CJA, NCJA (public), or NCJA (private), that enters into an agreement with a private contractor subject to the CJIS Security Addendum, The Security and Management Control Outsourcing Standard for Non-Channelers, or the Security and Management Control Outsourcing Standard for Channeling. The CA entering into an agreement with a contractor shall appoint an Agency Coordinator.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: The AC shall be responsible for the supervision and integrity of the system, training and continuing education of employees and operators, scheduling of initial training and testing, and certification testing and all required reports by NCIC.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: The AC shall:

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 1. Understand the communications, records capabilities, and needs of the Contractor which is accessing federal and state records through or because of its relationship with the CGA.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 2. Participate in related meetings and provide input and comments for system improvement.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 3. Receive information from the CGA (e.g., system updates) and disseminate it to appropriate Contractor employees.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 4. Maintain and update manuals applicable to the effectuation of the agreement, and provide them to the Contractor.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 5. Maintain up-to-date records of Contractor’s employees who access the system, including name, date of birth, social security number, date fingerprint card(s) submitted, date security clearance issued, and date initially trained, tested, certified or recertified (if applicable).

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 6. Train or ensure the training of Contractor personnel. If Contractor personnel access NCIC, schedule the operators for testing or a certification exam with the CSA staff, or AC staff with permission from the CSA staff. Schedule new operators for the certification exam within six (6) months of assignment. Schedule certified operators for biennial re- certification testing within thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of certification. Schedule operators for other mandated class.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 7. The AC will not permit an untrained/untested or non-certified Contractor employee to access CJI or systems supporting CJI where access to CJI can be gained.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 8. Where appropriate, ensure compliance by the Contractor with NCIC validation requirements.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 9. Provide completed applicant fingerprint cards on each Contractor employee who accesses the system to the CJA (or, where appropriate, CSA) for criminal background investigation prior to such employee accessing the system.

title: Agency Coordinator (AC)
shall_text: 10. Any other responsibility for the AC promulgated by the FBI.

title: CJIS System Agency Information Secrurity Officer (CSA ISO)
shall_text: The CSA ISO shall:

title: CJIS System Agency Information Secrurity Officer (CSA ISO)
shall_text: 1. Serve as the security point of contact (POC) to the FBI CJIS Division ISO.

title: CJIS System Agency Information Secrurity Officer (CSA ISO)
shall_text: 2. Document technical compliance with the CJIS Security Policy with the goal to assure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of criminal justice information to the user community throughout the CSA’s user community, to include the local level.

title: CJIS System Agency Information Secrurity Officer (CSA ISO)
shall_text: 3. Document and provide assistance for implementing the security-related controls for the Interface Agency and its users.

title: CJIS System Agency Information Secrurity Officer (CSA ISO)
shall_text: 4. Establish a security incident response and reporting procedure to discover, investigate, document, and report to the CSA, the affected criminal justice agency, and the FBI CJIS Division ISO major incidents that significantly endanger the security or integrity of CJI.

title: Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities
shall_text: Each Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities (i.e., LASO, ARSO, Security Point of Contact, etc.) shall:

title: Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities
shall_text: 1. Identify who is using the CSA approved hardware, software, and firmware and ensure no unauthorized individuals or processes have access to the same.

title: Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities
shall_text: 2. Identify and document how the equipment is connected to the state system.

title: Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities
shall_text: 3. Ensure that personnel security screening procedures are being followed as stated in this policy.

title: Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities
shall_text: 4. Ensure the approved and appropriate security measures are in place and working as expected.

title: Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities
shall_text: 5. Support policy compliance and ensure CSA ISO is promptly informed of security incidents.

title: FBI CJIS Division Information Security Officer (FBI CJIS ISO)
shall_text: The FBI CJIS ISO shall:

title: FBI CJIS Division Information Security Officer (FBI CJIS ISO)
shall_text: 1. Maintain the CJIS Security Policy.

title: FBI CJIS Division Information Security Officer (FBI CJIS ISO)
shall_text: 2. Disseminate the FBI Director approved CJIS Security Policy.

title: FBI CJIS Division Information Security Officer (FBI CJIS ISO)
shall_text: 3. Serve as a liaison with the CSA’s ISO and with other personnel across the CJIS community and in this regard provide technical guidance as to the intent and implementation of operational and technical policy issues.

title: FBI CJIS Division Information Security Officer (FBI CJIS ISO)
shall_text: 4. Serve as a point-of-contact (POC) for computer incident notification and distribution of security alerts to the CSOs and ISOs.

title: FBI CJIS Division Information Security Officer (FBI CJIS ISO)
shall_text: 5. Assist with developing audit compliance guidelines as well as identifying and reconciling security-related issues.

title: FBI CJIS Division Information Security Officer (FBI CJIS ISO)
shall_text: 6. Develop and participate in information security training programs for the CSOs and ISOs, and provide a means by which to acquire feedback to measure the effectiveness and success of such training.

title: FBI CJIS Division Information Security Officer (FBI CJIS ISO)
shall_text: 7. Maintain a security policy resource center (SPRC) on FBI.gov and keep the CSOs and ISOs updated on pertinent information.

title: State Compact Officer (SCO)
shall_text: Pursuant to the National Crime Prevention and Privacy Compact, each party state shall appoint a Compact Officer… ...Compact Officer who shall ensure that Compact provisions and rules, procedures, and standards established by the Compact Council are complied with in their respective state.

title: Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
shall_text: PII shall be extracted from CJI for the purpose of official business only.

title: Personally Identifiable Information (PII)
shall_text: Agencies shall develop policies, based on state and local privacy rules, to ensure appropriate controls are applied when handling PII extracted from CJI.

title: Policy Area 1: Information Exchange Agreements
shall_text: The information shared through communication mediums shall be protected with appropriate security safeguards.

title: Information Exchange
shall_text: Before exchanging CJI, agencies shall put formal agreements in place that specify security controls.

title: Information Exchange
shall_text: Information exchange agreements for agencies sharing CJI data that is sent to and/or received from the FBI CJIS shall specify the security controls and conditions described in this document.

title: Information Exchange
shall_text: Information exchange agreements shall be supported by documentation committing both parties to the terms of information exchange.

title: Monitoring, Review, and Delivery of Services
shall_text: As specified in the inter-agency agreements, MCAs, and contractual agreements with private contractors, the services, reports and records provided by the service provider shall be regularly monitored and reviewed.

title: Monitoring, Review, and Delivery of Services
shall_text: The CJA, authorized agency, or FBI shall maintain sufficient overall control and visibility into all security aspects to include, but not limited to, identification of vulnerabilities and information security incident reporting/response.

title: Monitoring, Review, and Delivery of Services
shall_text: The incident reporting/response process used by the service provider shall conform to the incident reporting/response specifications provided in this policy.

title: Managing Changes to Service Providers
shall_text: Any changes to services provided by a service provider shall be managed by the CJA, authorized agency, or FBI.

title: Managing Changes to Service Providers
shall_text: Evaluation of the risks to the agency shall be undertaken based on the criticality of the data, system, and the impact of the change.

shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to: organizational personnel with access control responsibilities

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level access control policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the access control policy and the associated access controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the access control policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current access control:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: (1) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | AUTOMATED SYSTEM ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT

title: (2) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | AUTOMATED TEMPORARY AND EMERGENCY ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT

title: (3) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | DISABLE ACCOUNTS

title: (3) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | DISABLE ACCOUNTS

title: (3) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | DISABLE ACCOUNTS
shall_text: (b) Are no longer associated with a user or individual;

title: (3) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | DISABLE ACCOUNTS

title: (4) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | AUTOMATED AUDIT ACTIONS
shall_text: Automatically audit account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions.

title: (5) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | INACTIVITY LOGOUT
shall_text: Require that users log out when a work period has been completed.

title: (13) ACCOUNT MANAGEMENT | DISABLE ACCOUNTS FOR HIGH-RISK INDIVIDUALS

title: ACCESS ENFORCEMENT
shall_text: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.

title: (14) ACCESS ENFORCEMENT | INDIVIDUAL ACCESS
shall_text: Provide automated or manual processes to enable individuals to have access to elements of their personally identifiable information.

title: INFORMATION FLOW ENFORCEMENT
shall_text: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems by preventing CJI from being transmitted unencrypted across the public network, blocking outside traffic that claims to be from within the agency, and not passing any web requests to the public network that are not from agency controlled or internal boundary protection devices (e.g., proxies, gateways, firewalls, or routers).

title: SEPARATION OF DUTIES
shall_text: a. Identify and document separation of duties based on specific duties, operations, or information systems, as necessary, to mitigate risk to CJI; and

title: SEPARATION OF DUTIES
shall_text: b. Define system access authorizations to support separation of duties.

title: LEAST PRIVILEGE
shall_text: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.

title: (1) LEAST PRIVILEGE | AUTHORIZE ACCESS TO SECURITY FUNCTIONS
shall_text: Authorize access for personnel including, security administrators, system and network administrators, and other privileged users with access to system control, monitoring, or administration functions (e.g., system administrators, information security personnel, maintainers, system programmers, etc.) to:

title: (1) LEAST PRIVILEGE | AUTHORIZE ACCESS TO SECURITY FUNCTIONS
shall_text: (a) Established system accounts, configured access authorizations (i.e., permissions, privileges), set events to be audited, set intrusion detection parameters, and other security functions; and

title: (1) LEAST PRIVILEGE | AUTHORIZE ACCESS TO SECURITY FUNCTIONS
shall_text: (b) Security-relevant information in hardware, software, and firmware.

title: (2) LEAST PRIVILEGE | NON- PRIVILEGED ACCESS FOR NONSECURITY FUNCTIONS
shall_text: Require that users of system accounts (or roles) with access to privileged security functionsorsecurity-relevantinformation(e.g.,auditlogs),usenon-privilegedaccountsor roles, when accessing nonsecurity functions.

title: (5) LEAST PRIVILEGE | PRIVILEGED ACCOUNTS
shall_text: Restrict privileged accounts on the system to privileged users.

title: (7) LEAST PRIVILEGE | REVIEW OF USER PRIVILEGES
shall_text: a. Reviews annually the privileges assigned to non-privileged and privileged users to validate the need for such privileges; and

title: (7) LEAST PRIVILEGE | REVIEW OF USER PRIVILEGES
shall_text: b. Reassign or remove privileges, if necessary, to correctly reflect organizational mission and business needs.

title: (9) LEAST PRIVILEGE | LOG USE OF PRIVILEGED FUNCTIONS
shall_text: Log the execution of privileged functions.

title: (10) LEAST PRIVILEGE | PROHIBIT NON-PRIVILEGED USERS FROM EXECUTING PRIVILEGED FUNCTIONS
shall_text: Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.

title: UNSUCCESSFUL LOGON ATTEMPTS
shall_text: a. Enforce a limit of five (5) consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a 15- minute time period; and

title: UNSUCCESSFUL LOGON ATTEMPTS
shall_text: b. Automatically lock the account or node until released by an administrator when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded.

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION
shall_text: a. Display a system use notification message to users before granting access to the system that provides privacy and security notices consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines and state that:

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION
shall_text: 1. Users are accessing a restricted information system;

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION
shall_text: 2. System usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit;

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION (continued)
shall_text: 3. Unauthorized use of the system is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION (continued)
shall_text: 4. Use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION (continued)
shall_text: b. Retain the notification message or banner on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit actions to log on to or further access the system; and

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION (continued)
shall_text: c. For publicly accessible systems:

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION (continued)
shall_text: 1. Display system use information consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, before granting further access to the publicly accessible system;

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION (continued)
shall_text: 2. Display references, if any, to monitoring, recording, or auditing that are consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems that generally prohibit those activities; and

title: SYSTEM USE NOTIFICATION (continued)
shall_text: 3. Include a description of the authorized uses of the system.

title: DEVICE LOCK
shall_text: a. Prevent further access to the system by initiating a device lock after a maximum of 30 minutes of inactivity and requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended.

title: DEVICE LOCK
shall_text: NOTE: In the interest of safety, devices that are: (1) part of a criminal justice conveyance; or (2) used to perform dispatch functions and located within a physically secure location; or (3) terminals designated solely for the purpose of receiving alert notifications (i.e., receive only terminals or ROT) used within physically secure location facilities that remain staffed when in operation, are exempt from this requirement.

title: DEVICE LOCK
shall_text: b. Retain the device lock until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures.

title: (1) DEVICE LOCK | PATTERN-HIDING DISPLAYS
shall_text: Conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image.

title: SESSION TERMINATION
shall_text: Automatically terminate a user session after a user has been logged out.

title: PERMITTED ACTIONS WITHOUT IDENTIFICATION OR AUTHENTICATION
shall_text: a. Identify any specific user actions that can be performed on the system without identification or authentication consistent with organizational mission and business functions; and

title: PERMITTED ACTIONS WITHOUT IDENTIFICATION OR AUTHENTICATION
shall_text: b. Document and provide supporting rationale in the security plan for the system, user actions not requiring identification or authentication.

title: REMOTE ACCESS
shall_text: a. Establish and document usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed; and

title: REMOTE ACCESS
shall_text: b. Authorize each type of remote access to the system prior to allowing such connections.

title: (1) REMOTE ACCESS | MONITORING AND CONTROL
shall_text: Employ automated mechanisms to monitor and control remote access methods.

title: (2) REMOTE ACCESS | PROTECTION OF CONFIDENTIALITY AND INTEGRITY USING ENCRYPTION
shall_text: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality and integrity of remote access sessions.

title: (3) REMOTE ACCESS | MANAGED ACCESS CONTROL POINTS
shall_text: Route remote accesses through authorized and managed network access control points.

title: (4) REMOTE ACCESS | PRIVILEGED COMMANDS AND ACCESS
shall_text: (a) Authorize the execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access only in a format that provides assessable evidence and for the following needs: compelling operational needs; and

title: (4) REMOTE ACCESS | PRIVILEGED COMMANDS AND ACCESS
shall_text: (b) Document the rationale for remote access in the security plan for the system.

title: WIRELESS ACCESS
shall_text: a. Establish configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of wireless access; and

title: WIRELESS ACCESS
shall_text: b. Authorize each type of wireless access to the system prior to allowing such connections.

title: (1) WIRELESS ACCESS | AUTHENTICATION AND ENCRYPTION
shall_text: Protect wireless access to the system using authentication of authorized users and agency- controlled devices, and encryption.

title: (3) WIRELESS ACCESS | DISABLE WIRELESS NETWORKING
shall_text: Disable, when not intended for use, wireless networking capabilities embedded within system components prior to issuance and deployment.

title: ACCESS CONTROL FOR MOBILE DEVICES
shall_text: a. Establish configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for organization-controlled mobile devices, to include when such devices are outside of controlled areas; and

title: ACCESS CONTROL FOR MOBILE DEVICES
shall_text: b. Authorize the connection of mobile devices to organizational systems.

title: (5) ACCESS CONTROL FOR MOBILE DEVICES | FULL DEVICE OR CONTAINER-BASED ENCRYPTION
shall_text: Employ full-device encryption to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on full- and limited-feature operating system mobile devices authorized to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: USE OF EXTERNAL SYSTEMS
shall_text: a. Establish agency-level policies governing the use of external systems consistent with the trust relationships established with other organizations owning, operating, and/or maintaining external systems, allowing authorized individuals to:

title: USE OF EXTERNAL SYSTEMS
shall_text: 1. Access the system from external systems; and

title: USE OF EXTERNAL SYSTEMS
shall_text: 2. Process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information using external systems; or

title: USE OF EXTERNAL SYSTEMS
shall_text: b. Prohibit the use of personally-owned information systems including mobile devices (i.e., bring your own device [BYOD]) and publicly accessible systems for accessing, processing, storing, or transmitting CJI.

title: (1) USE OF EXTERNAL SYSTEMS | LIMITS ON AUTHORIZED USE
shall_text: Permit authorized individuals to use an external system to access the system or to process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information only after:

title: (1) USE OF EXTERNAL SYSTEMS | LIMITS ON AUTHORIZED USE
shall_text: (a) Verification of the implementation of controls on the external system as specified in the organization’s security and privacy policies and security and privacy plans; or

title: (1) USE OF EXTERNAL SYSTEMS | LIMITS ON AUTHORIZED USE
shall_text: (b) Retention of approved system connection or processing agreements with the organizational entity hosting the external system.

title: (2) USE OF EXTERNAL SYSTEMS | PORTABLE STORAGE DEVICES — RESTRICTED USE
shall_text: Restrict the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems.

title: INFORMATION SHARING
shall_text: a. Enableauthorizeduserstodeterminewhetheraccessauthorizationsassignedtoa sharing partner match the information’s access and use restrictions as defined in an executed information exchange agreement; and

title: INFORMATION SHARING
shall_text: b. Employ attribute-based access control (see AC-2(d)(3)) or manual processes as defined in information exchange agreements to assist users in making information sharing and collaboration decisions.

title: PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE CONTENT
shall_text: a. Designate individuals authorized to make information publicly accessible;

title: PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE CONTENT
shall_text: b. Train authorized individuals to ensure that publicly accessible information does not contain nonpublic information;

title: PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE CONTENT
shall_text: c. Review the proposed content of information prior to posting onto the publicly accessible system to ensure that nonpublic information is not included; and

title: PUBLICLY ACCESSIBLE CONTENT
shall_text: d. Review the content on the publicly accessible system for nonpublic information quarterly and remove such information, if discovered.

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to all personnel when their unescorted logical or physical access to any information system results in the ability, right, or privilege to view, modify, or make use of unencrypted CJI:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 1. Organization-level awareness and training policy that:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the awareness and training policy and the associated awareness and training controls;

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security awareness and training responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the awareness and training policy nd procedures; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: c. Review and update the current awareness and training:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following changes in the information system operating environment, when security incidents occur, or when changes to the CJIS Security Policy are made; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following changes in the information system operating environment, when security incidents occur, or when changes to the CJIS Security Policy are made.

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: a. Provide security and privacy literacy training to system users (including managers, senior executives, and contractors):

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: 1. As part of initial training for new users prior to accessing CJI and annually thereafter; and

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: 2. When required by system changes or within 30 days of any security incident for individuals involved in the incident;

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: b. Employ one or more of the following techniques to increase the security and privacy awareness of system users:

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: 1. Displaying posters

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: 2. Offering supplies inscribed with security and privacy reminders

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: 3. Displaying logon screen messages

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: 4. Generating email advisories or notices from organizational officials

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: 5. Conducting awareness events

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: c. Update literacy training and awareness content annually and following changes in the information system operating environment, when security incidents occur, or when changes are made in the CJIS Security Policy; and

title: Literacy Training and Awareness
shall_text: d. Incorporate lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into literacy training and awareness techniques.

title: LITERACY TRAINING AND AWARENESS | INSIDER THREAT
shall_text: Provide literacy training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.

title: LITERACY TRAINING AND AWARENESS | SOCIAL ENGINEERING AND MINING
shall_text: Provide literacy training on recognizing and reporting potential and actual instances of social engineering and social mining.

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: a. Provide role-based security and privacy training to personnel with the following roles and responsibilities:

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: · All individuals with unescorted access to a physically secure location;

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: · General User: A user, but not a process, who is authorized to use an information system;

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: · Privileged User: A user that is authorized (and, therefore, trusted) to perform security- relevant functions that general users are not authorized to perform;

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: · Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities: Personnel with the responsibility to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of CJI and the implementation of technology in a manner compliant with the CJISSECPOL.

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: 1. Before authorizing access to the system, information, or performing assigned duties, and annually thereafter; and

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: 2. When required by system changes;

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: b. Update role-based training content annually and following audits of the CSA and local agencies ; changes in the information system operating environment; security incidents; or when changes are made to the CJIS Security Policy;

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: c. Incorporate lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into role-based training;

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: d. Incorporate the minimum following topics into the appropriate role-based training content:

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: 1. All individuals with unescorted access to a physically secure location:

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: a. Section 4.2 Access, Use and Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information (CHRI), NCIC Restricted Files Information, and NCIC Non-Restricted Files Information Penalties

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: b. IR-2 Incident Response Training

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: c. IR-6 Incident Reporting

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: d. PE-2 Physical Access Authorizations

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: e. PE-3 Physical Access Control

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: f. PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: g. PE-8 Visitor Access Records

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: h. PS-8 Personnel Sanctions

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: 2. General User: A user, but not a process, who is authorized to use an information system. In addition to AT-3 (d) (1) above, include the following topics:

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: a. Section 4.1 Criminal Justice Information

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: b. Section 4.2.3 Proper Access, Use, and Dissemination of NCIC Non-Restricted Files Information

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: c. Section 4.3 Personally Identifiable Information

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: d. AC-3 Access Enforcement

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: e. AC-6 Least Privilege

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: f. AC-8 System Use Notification

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: g. AC-11 Device Lock

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: h. AC-18 Wireless Access

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: i. AC-20 Use of External Systems

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: j. AT-2(3) Literacy Training and Awareness/Social Engineering and Mining

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: k. AU-6 Audit Record Review, Analysis and Reporting

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: l. CA-3 Information Exchange

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: m. IA-2 Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: n. IA-5(1)(a) Memorized Secret Authenticators and Verifiers

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: o. MP Media Protection

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: p. MP-2 Media Access

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING
shall_text: q. MP-4 Media Storage

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: r. PE-5 Access Control for Output Devices

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: s. SC-13 Cryptographic Protection

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: t. SC-28 Protection of Information at Rest

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: u. SI-3, 5.20.4.2 Malicious Code Protection

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: v. SI-8 Spam Protection

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: w. Section 5.20.1.2 Cellular Devices

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: x. Section 5.20.2 Mobile Device Management

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: 3. Privileged User: A user that is authorized (and, therefore, trusted) to perform security- relevant functions that general users are not authorized to perform. In addition to AT-3 (d) (1) and (2) above, include the following topics:

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: a. AC Access Control

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: b. CP-6 Alternate Storage Site

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: c. CP-9 System Backup

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: d. SC System and Communications Protection

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: e. SI-2 Flaw Remediation

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: f. Most recent changes to the CJIS Security Policy

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: 4. Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities: Personnel with the responsibility to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of CJI and the implementation of technology in a manner compliant with the CJISSECPOL. In addition to AT-3 (d) (1), (2), and (3) above, include the following topics:

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: a. Section 3.2.9 Organizational Personnel with Security Responsibilities

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: b. Authorized Recipient Security Officer Role

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: c. Additional state/local/tribal/territorial or federal agency roles and responsibilities

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: d. Summary of audit findings from previous state audits of local agencies

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING (continued)
shall_text: e. Findings from the last FBI CJIS Division audit

title: ROLE-BASED TRAINING | PROCESSING PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION
shall_text: Provide all personnel when their unescorted logical or physical access to any information system results in the ability, right, or privilege to view, modify, or make use of unencrypted CJI with initial and annual training in the employment and operation of personally identifiable information processing and transparency controls.

title: TRAINING RECORDS
shall_text: a. Document and monitor information security and privacy training activities, including security and privacy awareness training and specific role-based security and privacy training; and

title: TRAINING RECORDS
shall_text: b. Retain individual training records for a minimum of three years.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with audit and accountability responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency and system-level audit and accountability policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the audit and accountability policy and the associated audit and accountability controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the audit and accountability policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current audit and accountability:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: a. Identify the types of events that the system is capable of logging in support of the audit function: authentication, file use, user/group management, events sufficient to establish what occurred, the sources of events, outcomes of events, and operational transactions (e.g., NCIC, III);

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: b. Coordinate the event logging function with other organizational entities requiring audit- related information to guide and inform the selection criteria for events to be logged;

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: c. Specify the following event types for logging within the system:

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: All successful and unsuccessful:

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: 1. System log-on attempts

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: 2. Attempts to use:

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: a. Access permission on a user account, file, directory, or other system resource;

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: b. Create permission on a user account, file, directory, or other system resource;

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: c. Write permission on a user account, file, directory, or other system resource;

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: d. Delete permission on a user account, file, directory, or other system resource;

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: e. Change permission on a user account, file, directory, or other system resource.

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: 3. Attempts to change account passwords

title: EVENT LOGGING
shall_text: 4. Actions by privileged accounts (i.e., root, Oracle, DBA, admin, etc.)

title: EVENT LOGGING (continued)
shall_text: 5. Attempts for users to:

title: EVENT LOGGING (continued)
shall_text: a. Access the audit log file;

title: EVENT LOGGING (continued)
shall_text: b. Modify the audit log file;

title: EVENT LOGGING (continued)
shall_text: c. Destroy the audit log file;

title: EVENT LOGGING (continued)
shall_text: d. Provide a rationale for why the event types selected for logging are deemed to be adequate to support after-the-fact investigations of incidents; and

title: EVENT LOGGING (continued)
shall_text: e. Review and update the event types selected for logging annually.

title: CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS
shall_text: Ensure that audit records contain information that establishes the following:

title: CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS
shall_text: a. What type of event occurred;

title: CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS
shall_text: b. When the event occurred;

title: CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS
shall_text: c. Where the event occurred;

title: CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS
shall_text: d. Source of the event;

title: CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS
shall_text: e. Outcome of the event; and

title: CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS
shall_text: f. Identity of any individuals, subjects, or objects/entities associated with the event.

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: Generate audit records containing the following additional information:

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: a. Session, connection, transaction, and activity duration;

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: b. Source and destination addresses;

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: c. Object or filename involved; and

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: d. Number of bytes received and bytes sent (for client-server transactions) in the audit records for audit events identified by type, location, or subject.

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: e. The III portion of the log shall clearly identify:

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: 1. The operator

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: 2. The authorized receiving agency

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: 3. The requestor

title: (1) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | ADDITIONAL AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: 4. The secondary recipient

title: (3) CONTENT OF AUDIT RECORDS | LIMIT PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION ELEMENTS
shall_text: Limit personally identifiable information contained in audit records to the following elements identified in the privacy risk assessment: minimum PII necessary to achieve the purpose for which it is collected (see Section 4.3).

title: AUDIT LOG STORAGE CAPACITY
shall_text: Allocate audit log storage capacity to accommodate the collection of audit logs to meet retention requirements (AU-11).

title: RESPONSE TO AUDIT LOGGING PROCESS FAILURES
shall_text: a. Alert organizational personnel with audit and accountability responsibilities and system/network administrators within one (1) hour in the event of an audit logging process failure; and

title: RESPONSE TO AUDIT LOGGING PROCESS FAILURES
shall_text: b. Take the following additional actions: restart all audit logging processes and verify system(s) are logging properly.

title: AUDIT RECORD REVIEW, ANALYSIS, AND REPORTING
shall_text: a. Review and analyze system audit records weekly for indications of inappropriate or unusual activity and the potential impact of the inappropriate or unusual activity;

title: AUDIT RECORD REVIEW, ANALYSIS, AND REPORTING
shall_text: b. Report findings to organizational personnel with audit review, analysis, and reporting responsibilities and organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities; and

title: AUDIT RECORD REVIEW, ANALYSIS, AND REPORTING
shall_text: c. Adjust the level of audit record review, analysis, and reporting within the system when there is a change in risk based on law enforcement information, intelligence information, or other credible sources of information.

title: (1) AUDIT RECORD REVIEW, ANALYSIS, AND REPORTING | AUTOMATED PROCESS INTEGRATION
shall_text: Integrate audit record review, analysis, and reporting processes using automated mechanisms.

title: (3) AUDIT RECORD REVIEW, ANALYSIS, AND REPORTING | CORRELATE AUDIT RECORD REPOSITORIES
shall_text: Analyze and correlate audit records across different repositories to gain organization-wide situational awareness.

title: AUDIT RECORD REDUCTION AND REPORT GENERATION
shall_text: a. Supports on-demand audit record review, analysis, and reporting requirements and after- the-fact investigations of incidents; and

title: AUDIT RECORD REDUCTION AND REPORT GENERATION
shall_text: b. Does not alter the original content or time ordering of audit records.

title: (1) AUDIT RECORD REDUCTION AND REPORT GENERATION | AUTOMATIC PROCESSING
shall_text: Provide and implement the capability to process, sort, and search audit records for events of interest based on the following content: information included in AU-3.

title: TIME STAMPS
shall_text: a. Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records;

title: TIME STAMPS
shall_text: b. Record time stamps for audit records that meet hundredths of a second (i.e., hh:mm:ss:00) interval and that use Coordinated Universal Time, have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time, or that include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

title: PROTECTION OF AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: a. Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion; and

title: PROTECTION OF AUDIT INFORMATION
shall_text: b. Alert organizational personnel with audit and accountability responsibilities, organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities, and system/network administrators upon detection of unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of audit information.

title: (4) PROTECTION OF AUDIT INFORMATION | ACCESS BY SUBSET OF PRIVILEGED USERS
shall_text: Authorize access to management of audit logging functionality to only organizational personnel with audit and accountability responsibilities, organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities, and system/network administrators.

title: AUDIT RECORD RETENTION
shall_text: Retain audit records for a minimum of one (1) year or until it is determined they are no longer needed for administrative, legal, audit, or other operational purposes to provide support for after-the-fact investigations of incidents and to meet regulatory and organizational information retention requirements.

title: AUDIT RECORD GENERATION
shall_text: a. Provide audit record generation capability for the event types the system is capable of auditing as defined in AU-2a on all systems generating required audit logs;

title: AUDIT RECORD GENERATION
shall_text: b. Allow organizational personnel with audit record generation responsibilities, organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities, and system/network administrators to select the event types that are to be logged by specific components of the system; and

title: AUDIT RECORD GENERATION
shall_text: c. Generate audit records for the event types defined in AU-2c that include the audit record content defined in AU-3.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. An assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and the associated assessment, authorization, and monitoring controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current assessment, authorization, and monitoring:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following changes to the assessment criteria and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following changes to the assessment criteria.

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: a. Select the appropriate assessor or assessment team for the type of assessment to be conducted;

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: b. Develop a control assessment plan that describes the scope of the assessment including:

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: 1. Controls and control enhancements under assessment;

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: 2. Assessment procedures to be used to determine control effectiveness; and

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: 3. Assessment environment, assessment team, and assessment roles and responsibilities;

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: c. Ensure the control assessment plan is reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to conducting the assessment;

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: d. Assess the controls in the system and its environment of operation and any controls that have been impacted by evolving threats at least once every three years to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting established security and privacy requirements;

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: e. Produce a control assessment report that documents the results of the assessment; and

title: CONTROL ASSESSMENTS
shall_text: f. Provide the results of the control assessment report to the individual who executed the CJIS User Agreement or is in contract with the FBI.

title: (1) CONTROL ASSESSMENTS | INDEPENDENT ASSESSORS
shall_text: Employ independent assessors or assessment teams to conduct control assessments.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE
shall_text: a. Approve and manage the exchange of information between the agency system and external systems using the following agreements when applicable;

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE
shall_text: 1. Executed CJIS User Agreements

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE
shall_text: a. Each CSA, SIB, or IA shall execute a signed written agreement (see Appendix D.1) with the FBI CJIS Division stating their willingness to demonstrate conformity with the CJISSECPOL before accessing and consuming CJIS systems and services as set forth in the agreement.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE
shall_text: b. The agreement shall include the standards, audit, and sanctions governing utilization of CJIS systems and services.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE
shall_text: c. The FBI CJIS Division is authorized to periodically test the ability to penetrate the FBI’s network through the external connection or system upon proper notification of all signatories in the user agreement.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: 2. Criminal Justice Agency User Agreements

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: a. Any CJA receiving access to CJI shall enter into a signed written agreement with the appropriate signatory authority of the CSA providing the access.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: b. The written agreement shall specify the FBI CJIS systems and services to which the agency will have access, and the FBI CJIS Division policies to which the agency must adhere. These agreements shall include:

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: i. Audit

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: ii. Dissemination

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: iii. Hit confirmation

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: iv. Logging

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: v. Quality Assurance (QA)

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: vi. Screening (Criminal Justice Employment)

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: vii. Security viii. Timeliness

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: ix. Training

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: x. Use of the system

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: xi. Validation

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: 3. Agreements for Noncriminal Justice Use of CHRI

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: A CJA, NCJA (public), or NCJA (private) designated to request civil fingerprint- based background checks, with full consent of the individual to whom the background check is taking place, for noncriminal justice functions, shall be eligible for access to CHRI. Access shall be permitted when such designation is authorized pursuant to federal law or state statute approved by the U.S. Attorney General. The CJA, NCJA (public), or NCJA (private) receiving access to CHRI shall enter into signed written agreements with the appropriate signatory authority of the CSA, SIB, or authorized agency providing the access. The written agreement shall specify the policies to which the agency must adhere, which includes all pertinent areas of the CJISSECPOL. Each NCJA that directly access FBI systems shall allow the FBI to periodically test the ability to penetrate the FBI’s network through the external connection or system. A CJA, NCJA (public), or NCJA (private) authorized to access CHRI for noncriminal justice functions pursuant to federal law or state statute approved by the U.S. Attorney General (defined by the Compact Council as an Authorized Recipient), cannot make CHRI available to another governmental agency, nongovernmental agency, or private contractor to perform noncriminal justice administrative functions without implementation of one of the following:

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: a. Security and Management Control Outsourcing Standard for Non- Channelers. Implementation is applicable to noncriminal justice administrative functions that do not require a direct connection to the FBI for submission of fingerprints and receipt of CHRI. Examples include making fitness determinations, processing, storing, or destroying documents, and maintaining IT platforms that do not connect to CJIS systems. Prior to implementation, Authorized Recipients must request and receive written permission from the State Compact Officer, Chief Administrator of the state’s criminal history record repository, or the FBI Compact Officer, as applicable.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: b. Security and Management Control Outsourcing Standard for Channeling. Implementation is applicable only to Channeling functions performed by an FBI- approved Channeler that require a direct connection to the FBI for submission of fingerprints and receipt of CHRI. Prior to implementation, Authorized Recipients must request and receive written permission from the State Compact Officer, Chief Administrator of the state’s criminal history record repository, or the FBI Compact Officer, as applicable.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: c. Management Control Agreement or Security Addendum (see Appendix H) pursuant to Title 28, C.F.R., Section 20.33 (a) (6) or (7). Although by regulation implementation of a Management Control Agreement or the Security Addendum is applicable to the administration of criminal justice pursuant to that agreement performed on behalf of CJAs, under very limited circumstances, implementation may also be applicable to CJAs that obtain and use CHRI for noncriminal justice purposes. Implementation for noncriminal justice purposes is only applicable when another governmental agency or private contractor performs both criminal justice and noncriminal justice administrative functions involving access to CHRI on behalf of the CJA. It is important to note that if the servicing governmental agency or private contractor solely performs noncriminal justice administrative functions, then the CJA would be required to implement the Security and Management Control Outsourcing Standard for Non-Channeling.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: b. Document, as part of each exchange agreement, the interface characteristics, security and privacy requirements, controls, and responsibilities for each system, and the impact level of the information communicated; and

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: c. Review and update the agreements at least triennially or when responsibilities or signatories change.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: d. Secondary Dissemination

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: 1. Log the dissemination of CHRI when released to another authorized agency, and that agency was not part of the releasing agency’s primary information exchange agreement(s). If CJI does not contain CHRI and is not part of an information exchange agreement, then it does not need to be logged.

title: INFORMATION EXCHANGE (continued)
shall_text: 2. Validate the requestor of CJI in conformance with the local policy as an employee and/or contractor of a law enforcement agency or civil agency requiring the CJI to perform their mission; or a member of the public receiving CJI via authorized dissemination.

title: PLAN OF ACTION AND MILESTONES
shall_text: a. Develop a plan of action and milestones for the system to document the planned remediation actions of the organization to correct weaknesses or deficiencies noted during the assessment of the controls and to reduce or eliminate known vulnerabilities in the system; and

title: PLAN OF ACTION AND MILESTONES
shall_text: b. Update existing plan of action and milestones at least every six (6) months or when new information is available based on the findings from control assessments, independent audits or reviews, and continuous monitoring activities.

title: AUTHORIZATION
shall_text: a. Assign a senior official as the responsible official for the system;

title: AUTHORIZATION
shall_text: b. Assign the CSO, SIB Chief, or IA Official as the authorizing official for common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems;

title: AUTHORIZATION
shall_text: c. Ensure that the authorizing official for the system, before commencing operations:

title: AUTHORIZATION
shall_text: 1. Accepts the use of common controls inherited by the system; and

title: AUTHORIZATION
shall_text: 2. Authorizes the system to operate;

title: AUTHORIZATION
shall_text: d. Ensure that the authorizing official for common controls authorizes the use of those controls for inheritance by organizational systems;

title: AUTHORIZATION
shall_text: e. Update the authorizations at least every three (3) years.

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: Develop a system-level continuous monitoring strategy and implement continuous monitoring in accordance with the organization-level continuous monitoring strategy that includes:

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: a. Establishing the following system-level metrics to be monitored:

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 1. AC-2(g) Account Management

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 2. AC-17(1) Remote Access | Monitoring and Control

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 3. AT-4(a) Training Records

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 4. CM-3(f) Configuration Change Control

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 5. CM-6(d) Configuration Settings

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 6. CM-11(c) User-Installed Software

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 7. IR-5 Incident Monitoring

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 8. MA-2(b) Controlled Maintenance

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 9. MA-3(a) Maintenance Tool

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 10. MA-4(a) Nonlocal Maintenance

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 11. PE-3(d) Physical Access Control

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 12. PE-6 Monitoring Physical Access

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 13. PE-14(b) Environmental Controls

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 14. PE-16 Delivery and Removal

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 15. PS-7(e) External Personnel Security

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 16. SA-9(c) External System Services

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 17. SC-7(a) Boundary Protection

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 18. SC-7(24)(b) Boundary Protection | Personally Identifiable Information

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 19. SC-18(b) Mobile Code

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: 20. SI-4 System Monitoring

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: b. Establishing an ongoing frequency for monitoring and an ongoing frequency for assessment of control effectiveness;

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: c. Ongoing control assessments in accordance with the continuous monitoring strategy;

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: d. Ongoing monitoring of system and organization-defined metrics in accordance with the continuous monitoring strategy;

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: e. Correlation and analysis of information generated by control assessments and monitoring;

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: f. Response actions to address results of the analysis of control assessment and monitoring information; and

title: CONTINUOUS MONITORING
shall_text: g. Reporting the security and privacy status of the system to organizational personnel with information security, privacy responsibilities, and system/network administrators annually, when security events/incidents occur, and when requested.

title: (1) CONTINUOUS MONITORING | INDEPENDENT ASSESSMENT
shall_text: Employ independent assessors or assessment teams to monitor the controls in the system on an ongoing basis.

title: (4) CONTINUOUS MONITORING | RISK MONITORING
shall_text: Ensure risk monitoring is an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy that includes the following:

title: (4) CONTINUOUS MONITORING | RISK MONITORING
shall_text: a. Effectiveness monitoring;

title: (4) CONTINUOUS MONITORING | RISK MONITORING
shall_text: b. Compliance monitoring; and

title: (4) CONTINUOUS MONITORING | RISK MONITORING
shall_text: c. Change monitoring.

title: INTERNAL SYSTEM CONNECTIONS
shall_text: a. Authorize internal connections of components with the capability to process, store, or transmit CJI to the system;

title: INTERNAL SYSTEM CONNECTIONS
shall_text: b. Document, for each internal connection, the interface characteristics, security and privacy requirements, and the nature of the information communicated;

title: INTERNAL SYSTEM CONNECTIONS
shall_text: c. Terminate internal system connections when no longer required or authorized; and

title: INTERNAL SYSTEM CONNECTIONS
shall_text: d. Review at least annually the continued need for each internal connection.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with configuration management responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level configuration management policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the configuration management policy and the associated configuration management controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the configuration management policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current configuration management:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any hardware or software changes to systems which process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any hardware or software changes to systems which process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: BASELINE CONFIGURATION
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and maintain under configuration control, a current baseline configuration of the system;

title: BASELINE CONFIGURATION
shall_text: b. Develop, document, and maintain a current and complete topological drawing depicting the interconnectivity of the agency network to criminal justice information systems and services; and

title: BASELINE CONFIGURATION
shall_text: c. Review and update the baseline configuration and topological drawing of the system:

title: BASELINE CONFIGURATION
shall_text: 1. At least annually;

title: BASELINE CONFIGURATION
shall_text: 2. When required due to security-relevant changes to the system and/or security incidents occur; and

title: BASELINE CONFIGURATION
shall_text: 3. When system components are installed or upgraded.

title: (2) BASELINE CONFIGURATION | AUTOMATION SUPPORT FOR ACCURACY AND CURRENCY
shall_text: Maintain the currency, completeness, accuracy, and availability of the baseline configuration of the system using automated mechanisms such as configuration management tools, hardware, software, firmware inventory tools, and network management tools.

title: (3) BASELINE CONFIGURATION | RETENTION OF PREVIOUS CONFIGURATIONS
shall_text: Retain at least one (1) previous versions of baseline configurations of the system to support rollback.

title: (7) BASELINE CONFIGURATION | CONFIGURE SYSTEMS AND COMPONENTS FOR HIGH-RISK AREAS
shall_text: a. Issue devices (e.g., mobile devices) with CJISSECPOL compliant configurations to individuals traveling to locations that the organization deems to be of significant risk; and

title: (7) BASELINE CONFIGURATION | CONFIGURE SYSTEMS AND COMPONENTS FOR HIGH-RISK AREAS
shall_text: b. Apply the following controls to the systems or components when the individuals return from travel: examine the device for signs of physical tampering, purge and reimage disk drives and/or devices as required, and ensure all security controls are in place and functional

title: CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL
shall_text: a. Determine and document the types of changes to the system that are configuration- controlled;

title: CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL
shall_text: b. Review proposed configuration-controlled changes to the system and approve or disapprove such changes with explicit consideration for security and privacy impact analyses;

title: CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL
shall_text: c. Document configuration change decisions associated with the system;

title: CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL (continued)
shall_text: d. Implement approved configuration-controlled changes to the system;

title: CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL (continued)
shall_text: e. Retain records of configuration-controlled changes to the system for two (2) years;

title: CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL (continued)
shall_text: f. Monitor and review activities associated with configuration-controlled changes to the system; and

title: CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL (continued)
shall_text: g. Coordinate and provide oversight for configuration change control activities through personnel with configuration management responsibilities, a Configuration Control Board, or Change Advisory Board that convenes regularly or when hardware or software changes (i.e., updates, upgrades, replacements, etc.) to the information system are required.

title: (2) CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL | TESTING, VALIDATION, AND DOCUMENTATION OF CHANGES
shall_text: Test, validate, and document changes to the system before finalizing the implementation of the changes.

title: (4) CONFIGURATION CHANGE CONTROL | SECURITY AND PRIVACY REPRESENTATIVES
shall_text: Require organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities to be members of the Configuration Control Board or Change Advisory Board.

title: IMPACT ANALYSES
shall_text: Analyze changes to the system to determine potential security and privacy impacts prior to change implementation.

title: (2) IMPACT ANALYSES | VERIFICATION OF CONTROLS
shall_text: After system changes, verify that the impacted controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with regard to meeting the security and privacy requirements for the system.

title: ACCESS RESTRICTIONS FOR CHANGE
shall_text: Define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to the system.

title: CONFIGURATION SETTINGS
shall_text: a. Establish and document configuration settings for components employed within the system that reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements using established best practices and guidelines such as Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Secure Technical Implementation Guidelines (STIGs), Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks, or Federal Information Processing Standards;

title: CONFIGURATION SETTINGS
shall_text: b. Implement the configuration settings;

title: CONFIGURATION SETTINGS
shall_text: c. Identify, document, and approve any deviations from established configuration settings for system components that store, process, or transmit CJI based on operational requirements; and

title: CONFIGURATION SETTINGS
shall_text: d. Monitor and control changes to the configuration settings in accordance with organizational policies and procedures.

title: LEAST FUNCTIONALITY
shall_text: a. Configure the system to provide only essential capabilities to meet operational requirements; and

title: LEAST FUNCTIONALITY
shall_text: b. Prohibit or restrict the use of specified functions, ports, protocols, software, and/or services: which are not required.

title: (1) LEAST FUNCTIONALITY | PERIODIC REVIEW
shall_text: a. Review the system annually, as the system changes, or incidents occur to identify unnecessary and/or nonsecure functions, ports, protocols, software, and services; and

title: (1) LEAST FUNCTIONALITY | PERIODIC REVIEW
shall_text: b. Disable or remove functions, ports, protocols, software, and/or services within the system deemed to be unnecessary and/or unsecure.

title: (2) LEAST FUNCTIONALITY | PREVENT PROGRAM EXECUTION
shall_text: Prevent program execution in accordance with rules of behavior and/or rules authorizing the terms and conditions of software program usage.

title: (5) LEAST FUNCTIONALITY | AUTHORIZED SOFTWARE — ALLOW- BY-EXCEPTION
shall_text: a. Identify software programs authorized to execute on the system;

title: (5) LEAST FUNCTIONALITY | AUTHORIZED SOFTWARE — ALLOW- BY-EXCEPTION
shall_text: b. Employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy to allow the execution of authorized software programs on the system; and

title: (5) LEAST FUNCTIONALITY | AUTHORIZED SOFTWARE — ALLOW- BY-EXCEPTION
shall_text: c. Review and update the list of authorized software programs annually.

title: SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY
shall_text: a. Develop and document an inventory of system components that:

title: SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY
shall_text: 1. Accurately reflects the system;

title: SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY
shall_text: 2. Includes all components within the system;

title: SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY
shall_text: 3. Does not include duplicate accounting of components or components assigned to any other system;

title: SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY
shall_text: 4. Is at the level of granularity deemed necessary for tracking and reporting; and

title: SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY
shall_text: 5. Includes the following minimum information to achieve system component accountability: date of installation, model, serial number, manufacturer, supplier information, component type, software owner, software version number, software license information, and hardware and physical location; and

title: SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY
shall_text: b. Review and update the system component inventory annually.

title: (1) SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY | UPDATES DURING INSTALLATION AND REMOVAL
shall_text: Update the inventory of system components as part of component installations, removals, and system updates.

title: (3) SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY | AUTOMATED UNAUTHORIZED COMPONENT DETECTION
shall_text: a. Detect the presence of unauthorized hardware, software, and firmware components within the system using automated mechanisms continuously or at least weekly; and

title: (3) SYSTEM COMPONENT INVENTORY | AUTOMATED UNAUTHORIZED COMPONENT DETECTION
shall_text: b. Take the following actions when unauthorized components are detected: disable or isolate the unauthorized components and notify organizational personnel with security responsibilities.

title: CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: Develop, document, and implement a configuration management plan for the system that:

title: CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: a. Addresses roles, responsibilities, and configuration management processes and procedures;

title: CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: b. Establishes a process for identifying configuration items throughout the system development life cycle and for managing the configuration of the configuration items;

title: CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: c. Defines the configuration items for the system and places the configuration items under configuration management;

title: CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: d. Is reviewed and approved by organizational personnel with information security responsibilities and organizational personnel with configuration management responsibilities; and

title: CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: e. Protects the configuration management plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

title: SOFTWARE USAGE RESTRICTIONS
shall_text: a. Use software and associated documentation in accordance with contract agreements and copyright laws;

title: SOFTWARE USAGE RESTRICTIONS
shall_text: b. Track the use of software and associated documentation protected by quantity licenses to control copying and distribution; and

title: SOFTWARE USAGE RESTRICTIONS
shall_text: c. Control and document the use of peer-to-peer file sharing technology to ensure that this capability is not used for the unauthorized distribution, display, performance, or reproduction of copyrighted work.

title: USER-INSTALLED SOFTWARE
shall_text: a. Establish agency-level policies governing the installation of software by users;

title: USER-INSTALLED SOFTWARE
shall_text: b. Enforce software installation policies through automated methods; and

title: USER-INSTALLED SOFTWARE
shall_text: c. Monitor policy compliance through automated methods at least weekly.

title: INFORMATION LOCATION
shall_text: a. Identify and document the location of CJI and the specific system components on which the information is processed, stored, or transmitted;

title: INFORMATION LOCATION
shall_text: b. Identify and document the users who have access to CJI and system components where CJI is processed, stored, or transmitted; and

title: INFORMATION LOCATION
shall_text: c. Document changes to the location (i.e., system or system components) where CJI is processed, stored, or tansmitted.

title: (1) INFORMATION LOCATION | AUTOMATED TOOLS TO SUPPORT INFORMATION LOCATION
shall_text: Use automated tools to identify CJI on software and hardware system components to ensure controls are in place to protect organizational information and individual privacy.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with contingency planning responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level contingency planning policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the contingency planning policy and the associated contingency planning controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the contingency planning policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current contingency planning:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI, or training simulations or exercises; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI, or training simulations or exercises.

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: a. Develop a contingency plan for the system that:

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: 1. Identifies essential mission and business functions and associated contingency requirements;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: 2. Provides recovery objectives, restoration priorities, and metrics;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: 3. Addresses contingency roles, responsibilities, assigned individuals with contact information;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
