shall_text: 4. Addresses maintaining essential mission and business functions despite a system disruption, compromise, or failure;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: 5. Addresses eventual, full system restoration without deterioration of the controls originally planned and implemented;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: 6. Addresses the sharing of contingency information; and

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: 7. Is reviewed and approved by agency head or their designee;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: b. Distribute copies of the contingency plan to organizational personnel with contingency planning or incident response duties;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: c. Coordinate contingency planning activities with incident handling activities;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: d. Review the contingency plan for the system annually;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: e. Update the contingency plan to address changes to the organization, system, or environment of operation and problems encountered during contingency plan implementation, execution, or testing;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: f. Communicate contingency plan changes to organizational personnel with contingency planning or incident response duties;

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: g. Incorporate lessons learned from contingency plan testing, training, or actual contingency activities into contingency testing and training; and

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN
shall_text: h. Protect the contingency plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

title: (1) CONTINGENCY PLAN | COORDINATE WITH RELATED PLANS
shall_text: Coordinate contingency plan development with organizational elements responsible for related plans.

title: (3) CONTINGENCY PLAN | RESUME MISSION AND BUSINESS FUNCTIONS
shall_text: Plan for the resumption of essential mission and business functions within twenty-four (24) hours of contingency plan activation.

title: (8) CONTINGENCY PLAN | IDENTIFY CRITICAL ASSETS
shall_text: Identify critical system assets supporting essential mission and business functions.

title: CONTINGENCY TRAINING
shall_text: a. Provide contingency training to system users consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities:

title: CONTINGENCY TRAINING
shall_text: 1. Within thirty (30) days of assuming a contingency role or responsibility;

title: CONTINGENCY TRAINING
shall_text: 2. When required by system changes; and

title: CONTINGENCY TRAINING
shall_text: 3. Annually thereafter; and

title: CONTINGENCY TRAINING
shall_text: b. Review and update contingency training content annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI, or training simulations or exercises.

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN TESTING
shall_text: a. Test the contingency plan for the system annually using the following tests to determine the effectiveness of the plan and the readiness to execute the plan: checklists, walk-through and tabletop exercises, simulations (parallel or full interrupt), or comprehensive exercises.

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN TESTING
shall_text: b. Review the contingency plan test results; and

title: CONTINGENCY PLAN TESTING
shall_text: c. Initiate corrective actions, if needed.

title: (1) CONTINGENCY PLAN TESTING | COORDINATE WITH RELATED PLANS
shall_text: Coordinate contingency plan testing with organizational elements responsible for related plans.

title: ALTERNATE STORAGE SITE
shall_text: a. Establish an alternate storage site, including necessary agreements to permit the storage and retrieval of system backup information; and

title: ALTERNATE STORAGE SITE
shall_text: b. Ensure that the alternate storage site provides controls equivalent to that of the primary site.

title: (1) ALTERNATE STORAGE SITE | SEPARATION FROM PRIMARY SITE
shall_text: Identify an alternate storage site that is sufficiently separated from the primary storage site to reduce susceptibility to the same threats.

title: (3) ALTERNATE STORAGE SITE | ACCESSIBILITY
shall_text: Identify potential accessibility problems to the alternate storage site in the event of an area-wide disruption or disaster and outline explicit mitigation actions.

title: ALTERNATE PROCESSING SITE
shall_text: a. Establish an alternate processing site, including necessary agreements to permit the transfer and resumption of operations for essential mission and business functions within the time period defined in the system contingency plan(s) when the primary processing capabilities are unavailable;

title: ALTERNATE PROCESSING SITE
shall_text: b. Make available at the alternate processing site, the equipment and supplies required to transfer and resume operations or put contracts in place to support delivery to the site within the organization-defined time period for transfer and resumption; and

title: ALTERNATE PROCESSING SITE
shall_text: c. Provide controls at the alternate processing site that are equivalent to those at the primary site.

title: (1) ALTERNATE PROCESSING SITE | SEPARATION FROM PRIMARY SITE
shall_text: Identify an alternate processing site that is sufficiently separated from the primary processing site to reduce susceptibility to the same threats.

title: (2) ALTERNATE PROCESSING SITE | ACCESSIBILITY
shall_text: Identify potential accessibility problems to alternate processing sites in the event of an area-wide disruption or disaster and outlines explicit mitigation actions.

title: (3) ALTERNATE PROCESSING SITE | PRIORITY OF SERVICE
shall_text: Develop alternate processing site agreements that contain priority-of-service provisions in accordance with availability requirements (including recovery time objectives).

title: TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES
shall_text: Establish alternate telecommunications services, including necessary agreements to permit the resumption of system operations for essential mission and business functions within the time period as defined in the system contingency plan(s) when the primary telecommunications capabilities are unavailable at either the primary or alternate processing or storage sites.

title: (1) TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES | PRIORITY OF SERVICE PROVISIONS
shall_text: (a) Develop primary and alternate telecommunications service agreements that contain priority-of-service provisions in accordance with availability requirements (including recovery time objectives); and

title: (1) TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES | PRIORITY OF SERVICE PROVISIONS
shall_text: (b) Request Telecommunications Service Priority for all telecommunications services used for national security emergency preparedness if the primary and/or alternate telecommunications services are provided by a common carrier.

title: (2) TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES | SINGLE POINTS OF FAILURE
shall_text: Obtain alternate telecommunications services to reduce the likelihood of sharing a single point of failure with primary telecommunications services.

title: SYSTEM BACKUP
shall_text: a. Conduct backups of user-level information contained in operational systems for essential business functions as required by the contingency plans;

title: SYSTEM BACKUP
shall_text: b. Conduct backups of system-level information contained in the system as required by the contingency plans;

title: SYSTEM BACKUP
shall_text: c. Conduct backups of system documentation, including security- and privacy-related documentation as required by the contingency plans; and

title: SYSTEM BACKUP
shall_text: d. Protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of backup information.

title: (1) SYSTEM BACKUP | TESTING FOR RELIABILITY AND INTEGRITY
shall_text: Test backup information as required by the contingency plans to verify media reliability and information integrity.

title: (8) SYSTEM BACKUP | CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROTECTION
shall_text: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of CJI.

title: SYSTEM RECOVERY AND RECONSTITUTION
shall_text: Provide for the recovery and reconstitution of the system to a known state within the timeframe as required by the contingency plans after a disruption, compromise, or failure.

title: (2) SYSTEM RECOVERY AND RECONSTITUTION | TRANSACTION RECOVERY
shall_text: Implement transaction recovery for systems that are transaction-based.

title: Use of Originating Agency Identifiers in Transactions and Information Exchanges
shall_text: An FBI authorized originating agency identifier (ORI) shall be used in each transaction on CJIS systems in order to identify the sending agency and to ensure the proper level of access for each transaction.

title: Use of Originating Agency Identifiers in Transactions and Information Exchanges
shall_text: The original identifier between the requesting agency and the CSA/SIB/Channeler shall be the ORI, and other agency identifiers, such as user identification or personal identifier, an access device mnemonic, or the Internet Protocol (IP) address.

title: Use of Originating Agency Identifiers in Transactions and Information Exchanges
shall_text: Because the agency performing the transaction may not necessarily be the same as the agency requesting the transaction, the CSA/SIB/Channeler shall ensure that the ORI for each transaction can be traced, via audit trail, to the specific agency which is requesting the transaction.

title: Use of Originating Agency Identifiers in Transactions and Information Exchanges
shall_text: Agencies assigned a limited access ORI shall not use the full access ORI of another agency to conduct an inquiry transaction.

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to authorized personnel:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 1. Agency/Entity identification and authentication policy that:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the identification and authentication policy and the associated identification and authentication controls;

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the identification and authentication policy and procedures; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: c. Review and update the current identification and authentication:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
shall_text: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.

title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | Multi-Factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts
shall_text: Implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts.

title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | Multi-Factor Authentication to Non-Privileged Accounts
shall_text: Implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts.

title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) |Access to Accounts - Replay Resistant
shall_text: Implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to privileged and non- privileged accounts.

title: Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | Acceptance of PIV Credentials
shall_text: Accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials.

title: Device Identification and Authentication
shall_text: Uniquely identify and authenticate agency devices before establishing all remote and network connections. In the instance of local connection, the device must be approved by the agency and the device must be identified and authenticated prior to connection to an agency asset.

title: Identifier Management
shall_text: Manage system identifiers by:

title: Identifier Management
shall_text: a. Receiving authorization from organizational personnel with identifier management responsibilities to assign an individual, group, role, service, or device identifier;

title: Identifier Management
shall_text: b. Selecting an identifier that identifies an individual, group, role, service, or device;

title: Identifier Management
shall_text: c. Assigning the identifier to the intended individual, group, role, service, or device; and

title: Identifier Management
shall_text: d. Preventing reuse of identifiers for one (1) year.

title: Identifier Management | Identify User Status
shall_text: Manage individual identifiers by uniquely identifying each individual as agency or non- agency.

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: Manage system authenticators by:

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: a. Verifying, as part of the initial authenticator distribution, the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator;

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: b. Establishing initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization;

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: c. Ensuring that authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use;

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: d. Establishing and implementing administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution, for lost or compromised or damaged authenticators, and for revoking authenticators;

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: e. Changing default authenticators prior to first use;

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: f. Changing or refreshing authenticators annually or when there is evidence of authenticator compromise; changing or refreshing all other authenticator types as they expire or when there is evidence of authenticator compromise;

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: g. Protecting authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification;

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: h. Requiring individuals to take, and having devices implement, specific controls to protect authenticators; and

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: i. Changing authenticators for group or role accounts when membership to those accounts changes.

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: j. All credential service providers (CSPs) authenticating claimants at Authenticator Assurance Level 2 (AAL2) SHALL be assessed on the following criteria:

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: (1) Authentication SHALL occur by the use of either a multi-factor authenticator or a combination of two single-factor authenticators.

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: (2) If the multi-factor authentication process uses a combination of two single- factor authenticators, then it SHALL include a Memorized Secret authenticator and a possession-based authenticator. (NIST 800-63B, Section 4.2.1)

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: (3) Cryptographic authenticators used at AAL2 SHALL use approved cryptography.

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: (4) At least one authenticator used at AAL2 SHALL be replay resistant.

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: (5) Communication between the claimant and verifier SHALL be via an authenticated protected channel.

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: (6) Verifiers operated by federal government agencies at AAL2 SHALL be validated to meet the requirements of FIPS 140 Level 1.

title: Authenticator Management
shall_text: (7) Authenticators procured by federal government agencies SHALL be validated to meet the requirements of FIPS 140 Level 1.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (8) If a device such as a smartphone is used in the authentication process, then the unlocking of that device (typically done using a PIN or biometric) SHALL NOT be considered one of the authentication factors.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (9) If a biometric factor is used in authentication at AAL2, then the performance requirements stated in IA-5 m Biometric Requirements SHALL be met.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (10) Reauthentication of the subscriber SHALL be repeated at least once per 12 hours during an extended usage session.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (11) Reauthentication of the subscriber SHALL be repeated following any period of inactivity lasting 30 minutes or longer.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (12) The CSP SHALL employ appropriately tailored security controls from the moderate baseline of security controls defined in the CJIS Security Policy.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: The CSP SHALL ensure that the minimum assurance-related controls for moderate-impact systems are satisfied.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (13) The CSP SHALL comply with records retention policies in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (14) If the CSP opts to retain records in the absence of any mandatory requirements, then the CSP SHALL conduct a risk management process, including assessments of privacy and security risks to determine how long records should be retained and SHALL inform subscribers of that retention policy.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: k. Privacy requirements that apply to all CSPs, verifiers, and RPs.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (1) The CSP SHALL employ appropriately tailored privacy controls from the CJIS Security Policy.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (2) If the CSP processes attributes for purposes other than identity proofing, authentication, or attribute assertions (collectively “identity service”), related fraud mitigation, or to comply with law or legal process, then the CSP SHALL implement measures to maintain predictability and manageability commensurate with the associated privacy risk.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: l. General requirements applicable to AAL2 authentication process.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (1) CSPs SHALL provide subscriber instructions on how to appropriately protect a physical authenticator against theft or loss.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (2) The CSP SHALL provide a mechanism to revoke or suspend the authenticator immediately upon notification from subscriber that loss or theft of the authenticator is suspected.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (3) If required by the authenticator type descriptions in IA-5(1), then the verifier SHALL implement controls to protect against online guessing attacks.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (4) If required by the authenticator type descriptions in IA-5(1) and the description of a given authenticator does not specify otherwise, then the verifier SHALL limit consecutive failed authentication attempts on a single account to no more than 100.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (5) If signed attestations are used, then they SHALL be signed using a digital signature that provides at least the minimum security strength specified in the latest revision of 112 bits as of the date of this publication.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (6) If the verifier and CSP are separate entities (as shown by the dotted line in Figure 8 Digital Identity Model), then communications between the verifier and CSP SHALL occur through a mutually-authenticated secure channel (such as a client-authenticated TLS connection).

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (7) If the CSP provides the subscriber with a means to report loss, theft, or damage to an authenticator using a backup or alternate authenticator, then that authenticator SHALL be either a memorized secret or a physical authenticator.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (8) If the CSP chooses to verify an address of record (i.e., email, telephone, postal) and suspend authenticator(s) reported to have been compromised, then...The suspension SHALL be reversible if the subscriber successfully authenticates to the CSP using a valid (i.e., not suspended) authenticator and requests reactivation of an authenticator suspended in this manner.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (9) If and when an authenticator expires, it SHALL NOT be usable for authentication.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (10) The CSP SHALL have a documented process to require subscribers to surrender or report the loss of any physical authenticator containing attribute certificates signed by the CSP as soon as practical after expiration or receipt of a renewed authenticator.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (11) CSPs SHALL revoke the binding of authenticators immediately upon notification when an online identity ceases to exist (e.g., subscriber’s death, discovery of a fraudulent subscriber), when requested by the subscriber, or when the CSP determines that the subscriber no longer meets its eligibility requirements.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (12) The CSP SHALL have a documented process to require subscribers to surrender or report the loss of any physical authenticator containing certified attributes signed by the CSP within five (5) days after revocation or termination takes place.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: m. Biometric Requirements

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (1) Biometrics SHALL be used only as part of multi-factor authentication with a physical authenticator (something you have).

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (2) An authenticated protected channel between sensor (or an endpoint containing a sensor that resists sensor replacement) and verifier SHALL be established.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (3) The sensor or endpoint SHALL be authenticated prior to capturing the biometric sample from the claimant.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (4) The biometric system SHALL operate with an FMR [ISO/IEC 2382-37] of 1 in 1000 or better. This FMR SHALL be achieved under conditions of a conformant attack (i.e., zero- effort impostor attempt) as defined in [ISO/IEC 30107-1].

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (5) The biometric system SHALL allow no more than 5 consecutive failed authentication attempts or 10 consecutive failed attempts if PAD demonstrating at least 90% resistance to presentation attacks is implemented.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (6) Once the limit on authentication failures has been reached, the biometric authenticator SHALL either:

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: i. Impose a delay of at least 30 seconds before the next attempt, increasing exponentially with each successive attempt, or

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: ii. disable the biometric user authentication and offer another factor (e.g., a different biometric modality or a PIN/Passcode if it is not already a required factor) if such an alternative method is already available.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (7) The verifier SHALL make a determination of sensor and endpoint performance, integrity, and authenticity.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (8) If biometric comparison is performed centrally, then use of the biometric as an authentication factor SHALL be limited to one or more specific devices that are identified using approved cryptography.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (9) If biometric comparison is performed centrally, then a separate key SHALL be used for identifying the device.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (10) If biometric comparison is performed centrally, then biometric revocation, referred to as biometric template protection in ISO/IEC 24745, SHALL be implemented.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (11) If biometric comparison is performed centrally, all transmission of biometrics SHALL be over the authenticated protected channel.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (12) Biometric samples and any biometric data derived from the biometric sample such as a probe produced through signal processing SHALL be zeroized immediately after any training or research data has been derived

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: n. Authenticator binding refers to the establishment of an association between a specific authenticator and a subscriber’s account, enabling the authenticator to be used — possibly in conjunction with other authenticators — to authenticate for that account.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (1) Authenticators SHALL be bound to subscriber accounts by either issuance by the CSP as part of enrollment or associating a subscriber-provided authenticator that is acceptable to the CSP.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (2) Throughout the digital identity lifecycle, CSPs SHALL maintain a record of all authenticators that are or have been associated with each identity.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (3) The CSP or verifier SHALL maintain the information required for throttling authentication attempts.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (4) The CSP SHALL also verify the type of user-provided authenticator so verifiers can determine compliance with requirements at each AAL.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (5) The record created by the CSP SHALL contain the date and time the authenticator was bound to the account.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (6) When any new authenticator is bound to a subscriber account, the CSP SHALL ensure that the binding protocol and the protocol for provisioning the associated key(s) are done at AAL2.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (7) Protocols for key provisioning SHALL use authenticated protected channels or be performed in person to protect against man-in-the- middle attacks.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (8) Binding of multi-factor authenticators SHALL require multi-factor authentication (or equivalent) at identity proofing.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (9) At enrollment, the CSP SHALL bind at least one, and SHOULD bind at least two, physical (something you have) authenticators to the subscriber’s online identity, in addition to a memorized secret or one or more biometrics.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (10) At enrollment, authenticators at AAL2 and IAL2 SHALL be bound to the account.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (11) If the subscriber is authenticated at AAL1, then the CSP SHALL NOT expose personal information, even if self-asserted, to the subscriber.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (12) If enrollment and binding are being done remotely and cannot be completed in a single electronic transaction, then the applicant SHALL identify themselves in each new binding transaction by presenting a temporary secret which was either established during a prior transaction, or sent to the applicant’s phone number, email address, or postal address of record.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (13) If enrollment and binding are being done remotely and cannot be completed in a single electronic transaction, then long-term authenticator secrets are delivered to the applicant within a protected session.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (14) If enrollment and binding are being done in person and cannot be completed in a single physical encounter, the applicant SHALL identify themselves in person by either using a secret as described in IA-5 n (12) above, or through use of a biometric that was recorded during a prior encounter.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (15) If enrollment and binding are being done in person and cannot be completed in a single physical encounter, temporary secrets SHALL NOT be reused.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (16) If enrollment and binding are being done in person and cannot be completed in a single physical encounter and the CSP issues long-term authenticator secrets during a physical transaction, they SHALL be loaded locally onto a physical device that is issued in person to the applicant or delivered in a manner that confirms the address of record.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (17) Before adding a new authenticator to a subscriber’s account, the CSP SHALL first require the subscriber to authenticate at AAL2 (or a higher AAL) at which the new authenticator will be used.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (18) If the subscriber’s account has only one authentication factor bound to it, the CSP SHALL require the subscriber to authenticate at AAL1 in order to bind an additional authenticator of a different authentication factor.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (19) If a subscriber loses all authenticators of a factor necessary to complete multi- factor authentication and has been identity proofed at IAL2, that subscriber SHALL repeat the identity proofing process described in IA-12.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (20) If a subscriber loses all authenticators of a factor necessary to complete multi- factor authentication and has been identity proofed at IAL2 or IAL3, the CSP SHALL require the claimant to authenticate using an authenticator of the remaining factor, if any, to confirm binding to the existing identity.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (21) If the CSP opts to allow binding of a new memorized secret with the use of two physical authenticators, then it requires entry of a confirmation code sent to an address of record.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (22) If the CSP opts to allow binding of a new memorized secret with the use of two physical authenticators, then the confirmation code SHALL consist of at least 6 random alphanumeric characters generated by an approved random bit generator [SP 800-90Ar1].

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (23) If the CSP opts to allow binding of a new memorized secret with the use of two physical authenticators, then the confirmation code SHALL be valid for a maximum of 7 days but MAY be made valid up to 21 days via an exception process to accommodate addresses outside the direct reach of the U.S. Postal Service. Confirmation codes sent by means other than physical mail SHALL be valid for a maximum of 5 minutes.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: o. Session Management: The following requirements apply to applications where a session is maintained between the subscriber and relying party to allow multiple interactions without repeating the authentication event each time.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (1) Session Binding Requirements: A session occurs between the software that a subscriber is running — such as a browser, application, or operating system (i.e., the session subject) — and the RP or CSP that the subscriber is accessing (i.e., the session host).

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: a. A session is maintained by a session secret which SHALL be shared between the subscriber’s software and the service being accessed.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: b. The secret SHALL be presented directly by the subscriber’s software or possession of the secret SHALL be proven using a cryptographic mechanism.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: c. The secret used for session binding SHALL be generated by the session host in direct response to an authentication event.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: d. A session SHALL NOT be considered at a higher AAL than the authentication event.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: e. Secrets used for session binding SHALL be generated by the session host during an interaction, typically immediately following authentication.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: f. Secrets used for session binding SHALL be generated by an approved random bit generator [SP 800-90Ar1].

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: g. Secrets used for session binding SHALL contain at least 64 bits of entropy.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: h. Secrets used for session binding SHALL be erased or invalidated by the session subject when the subscriber logs out.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: i. Secrets used for session binding SHALL be sent to and received from the device using an authenticated protected channel.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: j. Secrets used for session binding SHALL time out and not be accepted after the times specified in IA-5(j)(10) and IA-5(j)(11) as appropriate for the AAL.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: k. Secrets used for session binding SHALL NOT be available to insecure communications between the host and subscriber’s endpoint.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: l. Authenticated sessions SHALL NOT fall back to an insecure transport, such as from https to http, following authentication.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: m. URLs or POST content SHALL contain a session identifier that SHALL be verified by the RP to ensure that actions taken outside the session do not affect the protected session.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: n. Browser cookies SHALL be tagged to be accessible only on secure (HTTPS) sessions.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: o. Browser cookies SHALL be accessible to the minimum practical set of hostnames and paths.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: p. Expiration of browser cookies SHALL NOT be depended upon to enforce session timeouts.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: q. The presence of an OAuth access token SHALL NOT be interpreted by the RP as presence of the subscriber, in the absence of other signals.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: (2) Reauthentication Requirements

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: a. Continuity of authenticated sessions SHALL be based upon the possession of a session secret issued by the verifier at the time of authentication and optionally refreshed during the session.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: b. Session secrets SHALL be non-persistent, i.e., they SHALL NOT be retained across a restart of the associated application or a reboot of the host device.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: c. Periodic reauthentication of sessions (at least every 12 hours per session) SHALL be performed to confirm the continued presence of the subscriber at an authenticated session.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: d. A session SHALL NOT be extended past the guidelines in IA-5 o (2) a – j based on presentation of the session secret alone.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: e. Prior to session expiration, the reauthentication time limit SHALL be extended by prompting the subscriber for the authentication factor(s) of a memorized secret or biometric.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: f. If federated authentication is being used, then since the CSP and RP often employ separate session management technologies, there SHALL NOT be any assumption of correlation between these sessions.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: g. An RP requiring reauthentication through a federation protocol SHALL — if possible within the protocol — specify the maximum (see IA-5 j (10)) acceptable authentication age to the CSP.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: h. If federated authentication is being used and an RP has specific authentication age (see IA-5 j (10)) requirements that it has communicated to the CSP, then the CSP SHALL reauthenticate the subscriber if they have not been authenticated within that time period.

title: Authenticator Management (continued)
shall_text: i. If federated authentication is being used, the CSP SHALL communicate the authentication event time to the RP to allow the RP to decide if the assertion is sufficient for reauthentication and to determine the time for the next reauthentication event.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (a) Memorized Secret Authenticators and Verifiers:

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (1) Maintain a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords via API or download from a third party. Update the list quarterly and when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly. Compare current memorized secrets against the list quarterly;

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (2) Require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery;

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (3) Allow user selection of long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters;

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (4) Employ automated tools to assist the user in selecting strong password authenticators;

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (5) If chosen by the subscriber, memorized secrets SHALL be at least 8 characters in length.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (6) If chosen by the CSP or verifier using an approved random number generator, memorized secrets SHALL be at least 6 characters in length.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (7) Truncation of the secret SHALL NOT be performed.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (8) Memorized secret verifiers SHALL NOT permit the subscriber to store a “hint” that is accessible to an unauthenticated claimant.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (9) Verifiers SHALL NOT prompt subscribers to use specific types of information (e.g., “What was the name of your first pet?”) when choosing memorized secrets.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (10) 10.(cid:9)When processing requests to establish and change memorized secrets, verifiers SHALL compare the prospective secrets against the list maintained as required by IA- 5(1)(a)(1) that contains values known to be commonly used, expected, or compromised.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (11) If a chosen secret is found in the list, the CSP or verifier SHALL advise the subscriber that they need to select a different secret.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (12) If a chosen secret is found in the list, the CSP or verifier SHALL provide the reason for rejection.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (13) If a chosen secret is found in the list, the CSP or verifier SHALL require the subscriber to choose a different value.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types
shall_text: (14) Verifiers SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber’s account to no more than five.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (15) Verifiers SHALL force a change of memorized secret if there is evidence of compromise of the authenticator.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (16) The verifier SHALL use approved encryption when requesting memorized secrets in order to provide resistance to eavesdropping and MitM attacks.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (17) The verifier SHALL use an authenticated protected channel when requesting memorized secrets in order to provide resistance to eavesdropping and MitM attacks.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (18) Verifiers SHALL store memorized secrets in a form that is resistant to offline attacks.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (19) Memorized secrets SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable one-way key derivation function.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (20) The salt SHALL be at least 32 bits in length and be chosen arbitrarily to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (21) Both the salt value and the resulting hash SHALL be stored for each subscriber using a memorized secret authenticator

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (22) If an additional iteration of a key derivation function using a salt value known only to the verifier is performed, then this secret salt value SHALL be generated with an approved random bit generator and of sufficient length.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (23) If an additional iteration of a key derivation function using a salt value known only to the verifier is performed, then this secret salt value SHALL provide at least the minimum- security strength.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (24) If an additional iteration of a key derivation function using a salt value known only to the verifier is performed, then this secret salt value SHALL be stored separately from the memorized secrets.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (b) Look-Up Secret Authenticators and Verifiers

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (1) CSPs creating look-up secret authenticators SHALL use an approved random bit generator to generate the list of secrets.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (2) Look-up secrets SHALL have at least 20 bits of entropy.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (3) If look-up secrets are distributed online, then they SHALL be distributed over a secure channel in accordance with the post-enrollment binding requirements in IA- 5(n)(16) through (22).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (4) Verifiers of look-up secrets SHALL prompt the claimant for the next secret from their authenticator or for a specific (e.g., numbered) secret.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (5) A given secret from an authenticator SHALL be used successfully only once.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (6) If a look-up secret is derived from a grid (bingo) card, then each cell of the grid SHALL be used only once.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (7) Verifiers SHALL store look-up secrets in a form that is resistant to offline attacks.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (8) If look-up secrets have at least 112 bits of entropy, then they SHALL be hashed with an approved one-way function

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (9) If look-up secrets have less than 112 bits of entropy, then they SHALL be salted and hashed using a suitable one-way key derivation function.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (10) If look-up secrets have less than 112 bits of entropy, then the salt SHALL be at least 32 bits in length and be chosen arbitrarily to minimize salt value collisions among stored hashes.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (11) If look-up secrets have less than 112 bits of entropy, then both the salt value and the resulting hash SHALL be stored for each look-up secret

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (12) If look-up secrets that have less than 64 bits of entropy, then the verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber’s account.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (13) The verifier SHALL use approved encryption when requesting look-up secrets in order to provide resistance to eavesdropping and MitM attacks.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (14) The verifier SHALL use an authenticated protected channel when requesting look- up secrets in order to provide resistance to eavesdropping and MitM attacks.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (c) Out-of-Band Authenticators and Verifiers

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (1) The out-of-band authenticator SHALL establish a separate channel with the verifier in order to retrieve the out-of-band secret or authentication request.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (2) Communication over the secondary channel SHALL be encrypted unless sent via the public switched telephone network (PSTN).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (3) Methods that do not prove possession of a specific device, such as voice-over-IP (VOIP) or email, SHALL NOT be used for out-of-band authentication.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (4) If PSTN is not being used for out-of-band communication, then the out-of-band authenticator SHALL uniquely authenticate itself by establishing an authenticated protected channel with the verifier.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (5) If PSTN is not being used for out-of-band communication, then the out-of-band authenticator SHALL communicate with the verifier using approved cryptography.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (6) If PSTN is not being used for out-of-band communication, then the key used to authenticate the out-of-band device SHALL be stored in suitably secure storage available to the authenticator application (e.g., keychain storage, TPM, TEE, secure element).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (7) If the PSTN is used for out-of-band authentication and a secret is sent to the out- of-band device via the PSTN, then the out-of-band authenticator SHALL uniquely authenticate itself to a mobile telephone network using a SIM card or equivalent that uniquely identifies the device.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (8) If the out-of-band authenticator sends an approval message over the secondary communication channel, it SHALL either accept transfer of a secret from the primary channel to be sent to the verifier via the secondary communications channel, or present a secret received via the secondary channel from the verifier and prompt the claimant to verify the consistency of that secret with the primary channel, prior to accepting a yes/no response from the claimant which it sends to the verifier.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (9) The verifier SHALL NOT store the identifying key itself, but SHALL use a verification method (e.g., an approved hash function or proof of possession of the identifying key) to uniquely identify the authenticator.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (10) Depending on the type of out-of-band authenticator, one of the following SHALL take place: transfer of a secret to the primary channel, transfer of a secret to the secondary channel, or verification of secrets by the claimant.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (11) If the out-of-band authenticator operates by transferring the secret to the primary channel, then the verifier SHALL transmit a random secret to the out-of-band authenticator and then wait for the secret to be returned on the primary communication channel.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (12) If the out-of-band authenticator operates by transferring the secret to the secondary channel, then the verifier SHALL display a random authentication secret to the claimant via the primary channel and then wait for the secret to be returned on the secondary channel from the claimant’s out-of- band authenticator.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (13) If the out-of-band authenticator operates by verification of secrets by the claimant, then the verifier SHALL display a random authentication secret to the claimant via the primary channel, send the same secret to the out-of-band authenticator via the secondary channel for presentation to the claimant, and then wait for an approval (or disapproval) message via the secondary channel.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (14) The authentication SHALL be considered invalid if not completed within 10 minutes.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (15) Verifiers SHALL accept a given authentication secret only once during the validity period.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (16) The verifier SHALL generate random authentication secrets with at least 20 bits of entropy.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (17) The verifier SHALL generate random authentication secrets using an approved random bit generator.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (18) If the authentication secret has less than 64 bits of entropy, the verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber’s account as described in IA-5 l (3) through (4).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (19) If out-of-band verification is to be made using the PSTN, then the verifier SHALL verify that the pre-registered telephone number being used is associated with a specific physical device.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (20) If out-of-band verification is to be made using the PSTN, then changing the pre- registered telephone number is considered to be the binding of a new authenticator and SHALL only occur as described in IA-5(n)(16) through (22).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (21) If PSTN is used for out-of-band authentication, then the CSP SHALL offer subscribers at least one alternate authenticator that is not RESTRICTED and can be used to authenticate at the required AAL.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (22) If PSTN is used for out-of-band authentication, then the CSP SHALL Provide meaningful notice to subscribers regarding the security risks of the RESTRICTED authenticator and availability of alternative(s) that are not RESTRICTED.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (23) If PSTN is used for out-of-band authentication, then the CSP SHALL address any additional risk to subscribers in its risk assessment.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (24) If PSTN is used for out-of-band authentication, then the CSP SHALL develop a migration plan for the possibility that the RESTRICTED authenticator is no longer acceptable at some point in the future and include this migration plan in its digital identity acceptance statement.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (d) OTP Authenticators and Verifiers

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (1) The secret key and its algorithm SHALL provide at least the minimum security strength of 112 bits as of the date of this publication.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (2) The nonce SHALL be of sufficient length to ensure that it is unique for each operation of the device over its lifetime.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (3) OTP authenticators — particularly software-based OTP generators —SHALL NOT facilitate the cloning of the secret key onto multiple devices.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (4) The authenticator output SHALL have at least 6 decimal digits (approximately 20 bits) of entropy.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (5) If the nonce used to generate the authenticator output is based on a real-time clock, then the nonce SHALL be changed at least once every 2 minutes.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (6) The OTP value associated with a given nonce SHALL be accepted only once.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (7) The symmetric keys used by authenticators are also present in the verifier and SHALL be strongly protected against compromise.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (8) If a single-factor OTP authenticator is being associated with a subscriber account, then the verifier or associated CSP SHALL use approved cryptography to either generate and exchange or to obtain the secrets required to duplicate the authenticator output.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (9) The verifier SHALL use approved encryption when collecting the OTP.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (10) The verifier SHALL use an authenticated protected channel when collecting the OTP.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (11) If a time-based OTP is used, it SHALL have a defined lifetime (recommended 30 seconds) that is determined by the expected clock drift — in either direction — of the authenticator over its lifetime, plus allowance for network delay and user entry of the OTP.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (12) Verifiers SHALL accept a given time-based OTP only once during the validity period.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (13) If the authenticator output has less than 64 bits of entropy, the verifier SHALL implement a rate-limiting mechanism that effectively limits the number of failed authentication attempts that can be made on the subscriber’s account as described in IA-5 l (3) through (4).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (14) If the authenticator is multi-factor, then each use of the authenticator SHALL require the input of the additional factor.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (15) If the authenticator is multi-factor and a memorized secret is used by the authenticator for activation, then that memorized secret SHALL be a randomly chosen numeric secret at least 6 decimal digits in length or other memorized secret meeting the requirements of IA-5 (1)(a).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (16) If the authenticator is multi-factor, then use of a memorized secret for activation SHALL be rate limited as specified in IA-5 l (3) through (4).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (17) If the authenticator is multi-factor and is activated by a biometric factor, then that factor SHALL meet the requirements of IA-5 m, including limits on the number of consecutive authentication failures.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (18) If the authenticator is multi-factor, then the unencrypted key and activation secret or biometric sample — and any biometric data derived from the biometric sample such as a probe produced through signal processing — SHALL be zeroized immediately after an OTP has been generated.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (19) If the authenticator is multi-factor, the verifier or CSP SHALL establish, via the authenticator source, that the authenticator is a multi-factor device.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (20) In the absence of a trusted statement that it is a multi-factor device, the verifier SHALL treat the authenticator as single-factor, in accordance with IA-5 (1) (d) (1) through (13).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (e) Cryptographic Authenticators and Verifiers (including single- and multi-factor cryptographic authenticators, both hardware- and software-based)

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (1) If the cryptographic authenticator is software based, the key SHALL be stored in suitably secure storage available to the authenticator application.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (2) If the cryptographic authenticator is software based, the key SHALL be strongly protected against unauthorized disclosure by the use of access controls that limit access to the key to only those software components on the device requiring access.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (3) If the cryptographic authenticator is software based, it SHALL NOT facilitate the cloning of the secret key onto multiple devices.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (4) If the authenticator is single-factor and hardware-based, secret keys unique to the device SHALL NOT be exportable (i.e., cannot be removed from the device).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (5) If the authenticator is hardware-based, the secret key and its algorithm SHALL provide at least the minimum-security length of 112 bits as of the date of this publication.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (6) If the authenticator is hardware-based, the challenge nonce SHALL be at least 64 bits in length.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (7) If the authenticator is hardware-based, approved cryptography SHALL be used.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (8) Cryptographic keys stored by the verifier SHALL be protected against modification.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (9) If symmetric keys are used, cryptographic keys stored by the verifier SHALL be protected against disclosure.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (10) The challenge nonce SHALL be at least 64 bits in length.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (11) The challenge nonce SHALL either be unique over the authenticator’s lifetime or statistically unique (i.e., generated using an approved random bit generator).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (12) The verification operation SHALL use approved cryptography.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (13) If a multi-factor cryptographic software authenticator is being used, then each authentication requires the presentation of the activation factor.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (14) If the authenticator is multi-factor, then any memorized secret used by the authenticator for activation SHALL be a randomly chosen numeric secret at least 6 decimal digits in length or other memorized secret meeting the requirements of IA-5 (1) (a).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (15) If the authenticator is multi-factor, then use of a memorized secret for activation SHALL be rate limited as specified in IA-5 l (3) through (4).

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (16) If the authenticator is multi-factor and is activated by a biometric factor, then that factor SHALL meet the requirements of IA-5 m, including limits on the number of consecutive authentication failures.

title: Authenticator Management | Authenticator Types (continued)
shall_text: (17) If the authenticator is multi-factor, then the unencrypted key and activation secret or biometric sample — and any biometric data derived from the biometric sample such as a probe produced through signal processing — SHALL be zeroized immediately after an authentication transaction has taken place.

title: Authenticator Management | Public Key Based Authentication
shall_text: (a) For public key-based authentication:

title: Authenticator Management | Public Key Based Authentication
shall_text: (1) Enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key; and

title: Authenticator Management | Public Key Based Authentication
shall_text: (2) Map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group; and

title: Authenticator Management | Public Key Based Authentication
shall_text: (b) When public key infrastructure (PKI) is used:

title: Authenticator Management | Public Key Based Authentication (continued)
shall_text: (1) Validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status information; and

title: Authenticator Management | Public Key Based Authentication (continued)
shall_text: (2) Implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation.

title: Authenticator Management | Protection of Authenticators
shall_text: Protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information to which use of the authenticator permits access.

title: Authentication Feedback
shall_text: Obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation and use by unauthorized individuals.

title: Cryptographic Module Authentication
shall_text: Implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines for such authentication.

title: Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users)
shall_text: Control: Uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users or processes acting on behalf of non-organizational users.

title: Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users) | Acceptance of PIV Credentials From Other Agencies
shall_text: Accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials from other federal, state, local, tribal, or territorial (SLTT) agencies.

title: Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users) | Acceptance of External Authenticators
shall_text: (a) Accept only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant; and

title: Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users) | Acceptance of External Authenticators
shall_text: (b) Document and maintain a list of accepted external authenticators.

title: Identification and Authentication (Non-Organizational Users) | Use of Defined Profiles
shall_text: Conform to the following profiles for identity management: Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) or OpenID Connect.

title: Re-Authentication
shall_text: Require users to re-authenticate when: roles, authenticators, or credentials change, security categories of systems change, the execution of privileged functions occur, or every 12 hours.

title: Identity Proofing
shall_text: a. Identity proof users that require accounts for logical access to systems based on appropriate identity assurance level requirements as specified in applicable standards and guidelines;

title: Identity Proofing
shall_text: b. Resolve user identities to a unique individual; and

title: Identity Proofing
shall_text: c. Collect, validate, and verify identity evidence.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence
shall_text: Require evidence of individual identification be presented to the registration authority.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification
shall_text: a. Require that the presented identity evidence be validated and verified through agency defined resolution, validation, and verification methods.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification
shall_text: b. Identity proofing SHALL NOT be performed to determine suitability or entitlement to gain access to services or benefits.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification
shall_text: c. 1. Collection of PII SHALL be limited to the minimum necessary to resolve to a unique identity in a given context.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification
shall_text: c. 2. Collection of PII SHALL be limited to the minimum necessary to validate the existence of the claimed identity and associate the claimed identity with the applicant providing identity evidence for appropriate identity resolution, validation, and verification.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: d. The CSP SHALL provide explicit notice to the applicant at the time of collection regarding the purpose for collecting and maintaining a record of the attributes necessary for identity proofing, including whether such attributes are voluntary or mandatory to complete the identity proofing process, and the consequences for not providing the attributes.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: e. If CSPs process attributes for purposes other than identity proofing, authentication, or attribute assertions (collectively “identity service”), related fraud mitigation, or to comply with law or legal process, then CSPs SHALL implement measures to maintain predictability and manageability commensurate with the privacy risk arising from the additional processing.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: f. If the CSP employs consent as part of its measures to maintain predictability and manageability, …then it SHALL NOT make consent for the additional processing a condition of the identity service.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: g. The CSP SHALL provide mechanisms for redress of applicant complaints or problems arising from the identity proofing.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: These [redress] mechanisms SHALL be easy for applicants to find and use.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: h. The CSP SHALL assess the [redress] mechanisms for their efficacy in achieving resolution of complaints or problems.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: i. The identity proofing and enrollment processes SHALL be performed according to an applicable written policy or *practice statement* that specifies the particular steps taken to verify identities.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: j. The *practice statement* SHALL include control information detailing how the CSP handles proofing errors that result in an applicant not being successfully enrolled.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: k. The CSP SHALL maintain a record, including audit logs, of all steps taken to verify the identity of the applicant as long as the identity exists in the information system.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: l. The CSP SHALL record the types of identity evidence presented in the proofing process.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: m. The CSP SHALL conduct a risk management process, including assessments of privacy and security risks to determine:

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 1. Any steps that it will take to verify the identity of the applicant beyond any mandatory requirements specified herein;

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 2. The PII, including any biometrics, images, scans, or other copies of the identity evidence that the CSP will maintain as a record of identity proofing (Note: Specific federal requirements may apply); and

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 3. The schedule of retention for these records (Note: CSPs may be subject to specific retention policies in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, or policies, including any National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) records retention schedules that may apply).

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: n. All PII collected as part of the enrollment process SHALL be protected to ensure confidentiality, integrity, and attribution of the information source.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: o. "The entire proofing transaction, including transactions that involve a third party, SHALL occur over authenticated protected channels. "

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: p. "If the CSP uses fraud mitigation measures, then the CSP SHALL conduct a privacy risk assessment for these mitigation measures. "

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: Such assessments SHALL include any privacy risk mitigations (e.g., risk acceptance or transfer, limited retention, use limitations, notice) or other technological mitigations (e.g., cryptography), and be documented per requirement IA-12(3) k – m above.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: q. In the event a CSP ceases to conduct identity proofing and enrollment processes, then the CSP SHALL be responsible for fully disposing of or destroying any sensitive data including PII, or its protection from unauthorized access for the duration of retention.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: r. Regardless of whether the CSP is a federal agency or non- federal entity, the following requirements apply to the federal agency offering or using the proofing service:

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 1. The agency SHALL consult with their Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP) to conduct an analysis determining whether the collection of PII to conduct identity proofing triggers Privacy Act requirements.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 2. The agency SHALL publish a System of Records Notice (SORN) to cover such collection, as applicable.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 3. The agency SHALL consult with their SAOP to conduct an analysis determining whether the collection of PII to conduct identity proofing triggers E-Government Act of 2002 requirements.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 4. The agency SHALL publish a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) to cover such collection, as applicable.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: s. An enrollment code SHALL be comprised of one of the following:

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 1. Minimally, a random six character alphanumeric or equivalent entropy. For example, a code generated using an approved random number generator or a serial number for a physical hardware authenticator; OR

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 2. A machine-readable optical label, such as a QR Code, that contains data of similar or higher entropy as a random six character alphanumeric.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: t. Training requirements for personnel validating evidence SHALL be based on the policies, guidelines, or requirements of the CSP or RP.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: u. This criterion applies to CSPs that provide identity proofing and enrollment services to minors (under the age of 18):

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: If the CSP provides identity proofing and enrollment services to minors (under the age of 18), then…the CSP SHALL give special consideration to the legal restrictions of interacting with minors unable to meet the evidence requirements of identity proofing [to ensure compliance with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998 (COPPA), and other laws, as applicable]. "

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: Requirements v and w apply to the collection of biometric characteristics for in-person (physical or supervised remote) identity proofing and are mandatory at IAL3. These criteria also apply to CSPs that optionally choose to collect biometric characteristics through in- person identity-proofing identity proofing and enrollment at IAL2.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: v. The CSP SHALL have the operator view the biometric source (e.g., fingers, face) for presence of non-natural materials and perform such inspections as part of the proofing process.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: w. The CSP SHALL collect biometrics in such a way that ensures that the biometric is collected from the applicant, and not another subject. All biometric performance requirements in IA-5 m (1) through (12) apply.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: x. The CSP SHALL support in-person or remote identity proofing, or both.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: y. The CSP SHALL collect the following from the applicant:

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 1. One piece of SUPERIOR or STRONG evidence if the evidence’s issuing source, during its identity proofing event, confirmed the claimed identity by collecting two or more forms of SUPERIOR or STRONG evidence and the CSP validates the evidence directly with the issuing source; OR

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 2. Two pieces of STRONG evidence; OR

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: 3. One piece of STRONG evidence plus two pieces of FAIR evidence

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: z. The CSP SHALL validate each piece of evidence with a process that can achieve the same strength as the evidence presented (see ’z’ above). For example, if two forms of STRONG identity evidence are presented, each piece of evidence will be validated at a strength of STRONG.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: aa. The CSP SHALL verify identity evidence as follows:

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: At a minimum, the applicant’s binding to identity evidence must be verified by a process that is able to achieve a strength of STRONG.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: bb. For IAL2 remote proofing: The collection of biometric characteristics for physical or biometric comparison of the applicant to the strongest piece of identity evidence provided to support the claimed identity performed remotely SHALL adhere to all requirements as specified in IA-5 m.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: cc. Knowledge-based verification (KBV) SHALL NOT be used for in-person (physical or supervised remote) identity verification.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: dd. The CSP SHALL employ appropriately tailored security controls, to include control enhancements, from the moderate or high baseline of security controls defined in the CJIS Security Policy.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: The CSP SHALL ensure that the minimum assurance-related controls for moderate-impact systems are satisfied.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: ee. Supervised Remote Identity Proofing: Supervised remote identity proofing is intended to provide controls for comparable levels of confidence and security to in-person IAL3 identity proofing for identity proofing processes that are performed remotely. Supervised remote identity proofing is optional for CSPs; that is, if a CSP chooses to use supervised remote identity proofing, then the following requirements, (1) through (8), would apply.
