It should be noted that the term “supervised remote identity proofing” has specialized meaning and is used only to refer to the specialized equipment and the following control requirements, (1) through (8). In addition to those requirements presented in this document, as well as the applicable identity validation and verification requirements, CSPs that provide supervised remote identity proofing services must demonstrate conformance with the requirements contained in this section. The following requirements for supervised remote proofing apply specifically to IAL3. If the equipment/facilities used for supervised remote proofing are used for IAL2 identity proofing, the following requirements, (1) through (8), for supervised remote proofing do not apply. In this case, the requirements for conventional remote identity proofing are applicable.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (1) Supervised remote identity proofing and enrollment transactions SHALL meet the following requirements, in addition to the IAL3 validation and verification requirements specified in IA-12(3)s.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (2) The CSP SHALL monitor the entire identity proofing session, from which the applicant SHALL NOT depart — for example, by a continuous high-resolution video transmission of the applicant.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (3) The CSP SHALL have a live operator participate remotely with the applicant for the entirety of the identity proofing session.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (4) The CSP SHALL require all actions taken by the applicant during the identity proofing session to be clearly visible to the remote operator.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (5) The CSP SHALL require that all digital validation of evidence (e.g., via chip or wireless technologies) be performed by integrated scanners and sensors.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (6) The CSP SHALL require operators to have undergone a training program to detect potential fraud and to properly perform a supervised remote proofing session.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (7) The CSP SHALL employ physical tamper detection and resistance features appropriate for the environment in which it is located.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (8) The CSP SHALL ensure that all communications occur over a mutually authenticated protected channel.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: ff. Trusted Referee: The use of trusted referees is optional for CSPs; that is, if a CSP chooses to use trusted referees for identity proofing and enrollment, then the following requirements, (1) through (3) would apply. The use of trusted referees is intended to assist in the identity proofing and enrollment for populations that are unable to meet IAL2 identity proofing requirements, or otherwise would be challenged to perform identity proofing and enrollment process requirements. Such populations may include, but are not limited to:

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: · disabled individuals;

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: · elderly individuals;

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: · homeless individuals,

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: · individuals with little or no access to online services or computing devices;

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: · unbanked and individuals with little or no credit history;

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: · victims of identity theft;

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: · children under 18; and

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: · immigrants.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: In addition to those requirements presented in the General section of this document, as well as the applicable IAL requirements, CSPs that use trusted referees in their identity proofing services must demonstrate conformance with the requirements contained in this section.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (1) If the CSP uses trusted referees, then…The CSP SHALL establish written policy and procedures as to how a trusted referee is determined and the lifecycle by which the trusted referee retains their status as a valid referee, to include any restrictions, as well as any revocation and suspension requirements.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (2) If the CSP uses trusted referees, then…The CSP SHALL proof the trusted referee at the same IAL as the applicant proofing.

title: Identity Proofing | Identity Evidence Validation and Verification (continued)
shall_text: (3) If the CSP uses trusted referees, then…The CSP SHALL determine the minimum evidence required to bind the relationship between the trusted referee and the applicant.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: a. Require that a registration code or notice of proofing be delivered through an out-of- band channel to verify the users address (physical or digital) of record.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: b. The CSP SHALL confirm address of record.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: c. Valid records to confirm address SHALL be issuing source(s) or authoritative source(s).

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: Self-asserted address data that has not been confirmed in records SHALL NOT be used for confirmation.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: d. Note that IAL2-7 applies only to in-person proofing at IAL2.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: If the CSP performs in-person proofing for IAL2 and provides an enrollment code directly to the subscriber for binding to an authenticator at a later time, then the enrollment code…SHALL be valid for a maximum of seven (7) days.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: e. For remote identity proofing at IAL2:

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: The CSP SHALL send an enrollment code to a confirmed address of record for the applicant.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: f. For remote identity proofing at IAL2:

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: The applicant SHALL present a valid enrollment code to complete the identity proofing process.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: g. Note that the following enrollment code validity periods apply to enrollment codes sent to confirmed addresses of record for IAL2 remote in-person proofing only.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: Enrollment codes shall have the following maximum validities:

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: i. 10 days, when sent to a postal address of record within the contiguous United States;

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: ii. 30 days, when sent to a postal address of record outside the contiguous United States;

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: iii. 10 minutes, when sent to a telephone of record (SMS or voice);

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: iv. 24 hours, when sent to an email address of record.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: h. If the enrollment code sent to the confirmed address of record as part of the remote identity proofing process at IAL2 is also intended to be an authentication factor, then…it SHALL be reset upon first use.

title: (5) Identity Proofing | Address Confirmation
shall_text: i. If the CSP performs remote proofing at IAL2 and optionally sends notification of proofing in addition to sending the required enrollment code, then…The CSP SHALL ensure the enrollment code and notification of proofing are sent to different addresses of record.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to all personnel when their unescorted logical or physical access to any information system results in the ability, right, or privilege to view, modify, or make use of unencrypted CJI:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level incident response policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the incident response policy and the associated incident response controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the incident response

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current incident response:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE TRAINING
shall_text: a. Provide incident response training to system users consistent with assigned roles and responsibilities:

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE TRAINING
shall_text: 1. Prior to assuming an incident response role or responsibility or acquiring system access;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE TRAINING
shall_text: 2. When required by system changes; and

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE TRAINING
shall_text: 3. Annually thereafter; and

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE TRAINING
shall_text: b. Review and update incident response training content annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: (3) INCIDENT RESPONSE TRAINING | BREACH
shall_text: Provideincidentresponsetrainingonhowtoidentifyandrespondtoabreach,including the organization’s process for reporting a breach.

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE TESTING
shall_text: Testtheeffectivenessoftheincidentresponsecapabilityforthesystemannuallyusingthe following tests: tabletop or walk-through exercises; simulations; or other agency- appropriate tests.

title: (2) INCIDENT RESPONSE TESTING | COORDINATION WITH RELATED PLANS
shall_text: Coordinateincidentresponsetestingwithorganizationalelementsresponsibleforrelated plans.

title: INCIDENT HANDLING
shall_text: a. Implementanincidenthandlingcapabilityforincidentsthatisconsistentwiththe incident response plan and includes preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery;

title: INCIDENT HANDLING
shall_text: b. Coordinate incident handling activities with contingency planning activities;

title: INCIDENT HANDLING
shall_text: c. Incorporate lessons learned from ongoing incident handling activities into incident response procedures, training, and testing, and implement the resulting changes accordingly; and

title: INCIDENT HANDLING
shall_text: d. Ensure the rigor, intensity, scope, and results of incident handling activities are comparable and predictable across the organization.

title: (1) INCIDENT HANDLING | AUTOMATED INCIDENT HANDLING PROCESSES
shall_text: Supporttheincidenthandlingprocessusingautomatedmechanisms(e.g.,onlineincident management systems and tools that support the collection of live response data, full network packet capture, and forensic analysis).

title: INCIDENT MONITORING
shall_text: Track and document incidents.

title: INCIDENT REPORTING
shall_text: a. Require personnel to report suspected incidents to the organizational incident response capability immediately but not to exceed one (1) hour after discovery; and

title: INCIDENT REPORTING
shall_text: b. Report incident information to organizational personnel with incident handling responsibilities, and the CSO, SIB Chief, or Interface Agency Official, and FBI CJIS ISO.

title: (1) INCIDENT REPORTING | AUTOMATED REPORTING
shall_text: Report incidents using automated mechanisms.

title: (3) INCIDENT REPORTING | SUPPLY CHAIN COORDINATION
shall_text: Provide incident information to the provider of the product or service and other organizations involved in the supply chain or supply chain governance for systems or system components related to the incident.

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE ASSISTANCE
shall_text: Provide an incident response support resource, integral to the organizational incident response capability, that offers advice and assistance to users of the system for the handling and reporting of incidents.

title: (1) INCIDENT RESPONSE ASSISTANCE | AUTOMATION SUPPORT FOR AVAILABILITY OF INFORMATION AND SUPPORT
shall_text: Increasetheavailabilityofincidentresponseinformationandsupportusingautomated mechanisms described in the discussion.

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: a. Develop an incident response plan that:

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 1. Provides the organization with a roadmap for implementing its incident response capability;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 2. Describes the structure and organization of the incident response capability;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 3. Provides a high-level approach for how the incident response capability fits into the overall organization;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 4. Meets the unique requirements of the organization, which relate to mission, size, structure, and functions;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 5. Defines reportable incidents;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 6. Provides metrics for measuring the incident response capability within the organization;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 7. Defines the resources and management support needed to effectively maintain and mature an incident response capability;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 8. Addresses the sharing of incident information;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 9. Is reviewed and approved by the organization’s/agency’s executive leadership annually; and

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: 10. Explicitly designates responsibility for incident response to organizational personnel with incident reporting responsibilities and CSO or CJIS WAN Official.

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: b. Distribute copies of the incident response plan to organizational personnel with incident handling responsibilities;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: c. Update the incident response plan to address system and organizational changes or problems encountered during plan implementation, execution, or testing;

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: d. Communicate incident response plan changes to organizational personnel with incident handling responsibilities; and

title: INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN
shall_text: e. Protect the incident response plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

title: (1) INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN | BREACHES
shall_text: Include the following in the Incident Response Plan for breaches involving personally identifiable information:

title: (1) INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN | BREACHES
shall_text: (a) A process to determine if notice to individuals or other organizations, including oversight organizations, is needed;

title: (1) INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN | BREACHES
shall_text: (b) An assessment process to determine the extent of the harm, embarrassment, inconvenience, or unfairness to affected individuals and any mechanisms to mitigate such harms; and

title: (1) INCIDENT RESPONSE PLAN | BREACHES
shall_text: (c) Identification of applicable privacy requirements.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with system maintenance responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level maintenance policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the maintenance policy and the associated maintenance controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the maintenance policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current maintenance:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: a. Schedule,document,andreviewrecordsofmaintenance,repair,andreplacementon system components in accordance with manufacturer or vendor specifications and/or organizational requirements;

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: b. Approve and monitor all maintenance activities, whether performed on site or remotely and whether the system or system components are serviced on site or removed to another location;

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: c. Require that organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities explicitly approve the removal of the system or system components from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement;

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: d. Sanitize equipment to remove information from associated media prior to removal from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, replacement, or destruction;

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: e. Check all potentially impacted controls to verify that the controls are still functioning properly following maintenance, repair, or replacement actions; and

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: f. Include the following information in organizational maintenance records:

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: 1. Component name

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: 2. Component serial number

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: 3. Date/time of maintenance

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: 4. Maintenance performed

title: CONTROLLED MAINTENANCE
shall_text: 5. Name(s) of entity performing maintenance including escort if required.

title: MAINTENANCE TOOLS
shall_text: a. Approve, control, and monitor the use of system maintenance tools; and

title: MAINTENANCE TOOLS
shall_text: b. Review previously approved system maintenance tools prior to each use.

title: (1) MAINTENANCE TOOLS | INSPECT TOOLS
shall_text: Inspect the maintenance tools used by maintenance personnel for improper or unauthorized modifications.

title: (2) MAINTENANCE TOOLS | INSPECT MEDIA
shall_text: Check media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used in the system.

title: (3) MAINTENANCE TOOLS | PREVENT UNAUTHORIZED REMOVAL
shall_text: Prevent the removal of maintenance equipment containing organizational information by:

title: (3) MAINTENANCE TOOLS | PREVENT UNAUTHORIZED REMOVAL
shall_text: (a) Verifying that there is no organizational information contained on the equipment;

title: (3) MAINTENANCE TOOLS | PREVENT UNAUTHORIZED REMOVAL
shall_text: (b) Sanitizing or destroying the equipment;

title: (3) MAINTENANCE TOOLS | PREVENT UNAUTHORIZED REMOVAL
shall_text: (c) Retaining the equipment within the facility; or

title: (3) MAINTENANCE TOOLS | PREVENT UNAUTHORIZED REMOVAL
shall_text: (d) Obtaining an exemption from organizational personnel with system maintenance responsibilities explicitly authorizing removal of the equipment from the facility.

title: NONLOCAL MAINTENANCE
shall_text: a. Approve and monitor nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic activities;

title: NONLOCAL MAINTENANCE
shall_text: b. Allow the use of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic tools only as consistent with organizational policy and documented in the security plan for the system;

title: NONLOCAL MAINTENANCE
shall_text: c. Employ strong authentication in the establishment of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions;

title: NONLOCAL MAINTENANCE
shall_text: d. Maintain records for nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic activities; and

title: NONLOCAL MAINTENANCE
shall_text: e. Terminate session and network connections when nonlocal maintenance is completed.

title: MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL
shall_text: a. Establish a process for maintenance personnel authorization and maintain a list of authorized maintenance organizations or personnel;

title: MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL
shall_text: b. Verify that non-escorted personnel performing maintenance on the system possess the required access authorizations; and

title: MAINTENANCE PERSONNEL
shall_text: c. Designate organizational personnel with required access authorizations and technical competence to supervise the maintenance activities of personnel who do not possess the required access authorizations.

title: TIMELY MAINTENANCE
shall_text: Obtain maintenance support and/or spare parts for critical system components that process, store, or transmit CJI within agency-defined recovery time and recovery point objectives of failure.

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to authorized individuals:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 1. Agency-level media protection policy that:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among agency entities, and compliance; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the media protection policy and the associated media protection controls;

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the media protection policy and procedures; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: c. Review and update the current media protection:

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 1. Policy at least annually and following any security incidents involving digital and/or non- digital media; and

title: Policy and Procedures
shall_text: 2. Procedures at least annually and following any security incidents involving digital and/or non-digital media.

title: Media Access
shall_text: Restrict access to digital and non-digital media to authorized individuals.

title: Media Marking
shall_text: a. Mark system media indicating the distribution limitations, handling caveats, and applicable security markings (if any) of the information; and

title: Media Marking
shall_text: b. Exempt digital and non-digital media containing CJI from marking if the media remain within physically secure locations and controlled areas.

title: Media Storage
shall_text: a. Physically control and securely store digital and non-digital media within physically secure locations or controlled areas and encrypt CJI on digital media when physical and personnel restrictions are not feasible; and

title: Media Storage
shall_text: b. Protect system media types defined in MP-4a until the media are destroyed or sanitized using approved equipment, techniques, and procedures.

title: Media Transport
shall_text: a. Protect and control digital and non-digital media to help prevent compromise of the data during transport outside of the physically secure locations or controlled areas using encryption, as defined in Systems and Communications Protection (SC). Physical media will be protected at the same level as the information would be protected in electronic form. Restrict the activities associated with transport of electronic and physical media to authorized personnel;

title: Media Transport
shall_text: b. Maintain accountability for system media during transport outside of the physically secure location or controlled areas;

title: Media Transport
shall_text: c. Document activities associated with the transport of system media; and

title: Media Transport
shall_text: d. Restrict the activities associated with the transport of system media to authorized personnel.

title: Media Sanitization
shall_text: a. Sanitize or destroy digital media prior to disposal, release out of agency control, or release for reuse using overwrite technology at least three times or degaussing. Inoperable digital media will be destroyed. Non-digital media will be securely disposed of when no longer needed for investigative or security purposes, whichever is later. Non- digital media will be destroyed by crosscut shredding or incineration; and

title: Media Sanitization (continued)
shall_text: b. Employ sanitization mechanisms with the strength and integrity commensurate with the security category or classification of the information.

title: Media Use
shall_text: a. Restrict the use of digital and non-digital media on agency-owned systems that have been approved for use in the storage, processing, or transmission of criminal justice information by using technical, physical, or administrative controls (examples below); and

title: Media Use
shall_text: b. Prohibit the use of personally-owned digital media devices on all agency-owned or controlled systems that store, process, or transmit criminal justice information; and

title: Media Use
shall_text: c. Prohibit the use of digital media devices on all agency-owned or controlled systems that store, process, or transmit criminal justice information when such devices have no identifiable owner.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with physical and environmental protection responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level physical and environmental protection policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the physical and environmental protection policy and the associated physical and environmental protection controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the physical and environmental protection policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current physical and environmental protection:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any physical, environmental, or security related incidents involving CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any physical, environmental, or security related incidents involving CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS AUTHORIZATIONS
shall_text: a. Develop, approve, and maintain a list of individuals with authorized access to the facility where the system resides;

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS AUTHORIZATIONS
shall_text: b. Issue authorization credentials for facility access;

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS AUTHORIZATIONS
shall_text: c. Review the access list detailing authorized facility access by individuals annually and when personnel changes occur; and

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS AUTHORIZATIONS
shall_text: d. Remove individuals from the facility access list when access is no longer required.

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: a. Enforce physical access authorizations by:

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: 1. Verifying individual access authorizations before granting access to the facility; and

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: 2. Controlling ingress to the facility using agency-implemented procedures and controls;

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: b. Maintain physical access audit logs for the physically secure location and agency- defined sensitive areas;

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: c. Control access to areas within the facility designated as non-publicly accessible by implementing physical access devices including, but not limited to keys, locks, combinations, biometric readers, placards, and/or card readers;

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: d. Escort visitors and control visitor activity in all physically secure locations;

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: e. Secure keys, combinations, and other physical access devices;

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: f. Inventory all agency-issued physical access devices annually; and

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: g. Change combinations and keys when keys are lost, combinations are compromised, or when individuals possessing the keys or combinations are transferred or terminated.

title: PHYSICAL ACCESS CONTROL
shall_text: h. If the above conditions cannot be met refer to the requirements listed in PE-17.

title: ACCESS CONTROL FOR TRANSMISSION
shall_text: Control physical access to information system distribution and transmission lines and devices within organizational facilities using agency-implemented procedures and controls.

title: ACCESS CONTROL FOR OUTPUT DEVICES
shall_text: Control physical access to output from monitors, printers, scanners, audio devices, facsimile machines, and copiers to prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining the output.

title: MONITORING PHYSICAL ACCESS
shall_text: a. Monitor physical access to the facility where the system resides to detect and respond to physical security incidents;

title: MONITORING PHYSICAL ACCESS
shall_text: b. Review physical access logs quarterly and upon occurrence of any physical, environmental, or security-related incidents involving CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: MONITORING PHYSICAL ACCESS
shall_text: c. Coordinate results of reviews and investigations with the organizational incident response capability.

title: (1) MONITORING PHYSICAL ACCESS | INTRUSION ALARMS AND SURVEILLANCE EQUIPMENT
shall_text: Monitor physical access to the facility where the system resides using physical intrusion alarms and surveillance equipment.

title: VISITOR ACCESS RECORDS
shall_text: a. Maintain visitor access records to the facility where the system resides for one (1) year;

title: VISITOR ACCESS RECORDS
shall_text: b. Review visitor access records quarterly; and

title: VISITOR ACCESS RECORDS
shall_text: c. Report anomalies in visitor access records to organizational personnel with physical and environmental protection responsibilities and organizational personnel with information security responsibilities.

title: (3) VISITOR ACCESS RECORDS | LIMIT PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION ELEMENTS
shall_text: Limit personally identifiable information contained in visitor access records to the minimum PII necessary to achieve the purpose for which it is collected (see Section 4.3).

title: (3) VISITOR ACCESS RECORDS | LIMIT PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION ELEMENTS
shall_text: Note: Access to visitor access records is restricted to authorized agency personnel.

title: POWER EQUIPMENT AND CABLING
shall_text: Protect power equipment and power cabling for the system from damage and destruction.

title: EMERGENCY SHUTOFF
shall_text: a. Provide the capability of shutting off power to all information systems in emergency situations;

title: EMERGENCY SHUTOFF
shall_text: b. Place emergency shutoff switches or devices in easily accessible locations to facilitate access for authorized personnel; and

title: EMERGENCY SHUTOFF
shall_text: c. Protect emergency power shutoff capability from unauthorized activation.

title: EMERGENCY POWER
shall_text: Provide an uninterruptible power supply to facilitate an orderly shutdown of the information system or transition of the information system to an alternate power source in the event of a primary power source loss.

title: EMERGENCY LIGHTING
shall_text: Employ and maintain automatic emergency lighting for the system that activates in the event of a power outage or disruption and that covers emergency exits and evacuation routes within the facility.

title: FIRE PROTECTION
shall_text: Employ and maintain fire detection and suppression systems that are supported by an independent energy source.

title: (1) FIRE PROTECTION | DETECTION SYSTEMS — AUTOMATIC ACTIVATION AND NOTIFICATION
shall_text: Employ fire detection systems that activate automatically and notify organizational personnel with physical and environmental protection responsibilities and police, fire, or emergency medical personnel in the event of a fire.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROLS
shall_text: a. Maintain adequate HVAC levels within the facility where the system resides at recommended system manufacturer levels; and

title: ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROLS
shall_text: b. Monitor environmental control levels continuously.

title: WATER DAMAGE PROTECTION
shall_text: Protect the system from damage resulting from water leakage by providing master shutoff or isolation valves that are accessible, working properly, and known to key personnel.

title: DELIVERY AND REMOVAL
shall_text: a. Authorize and control information system-related components entering and exiting the facility; and

title: DELIVERY AND REMOVAL
shall_text: b. Maintain records of the system components.

title: ALTERNATE WORK SITE
shall_text: a. Determine and document all alternate facilities or locations allowed for use by employees;

title: ALTERNATE WORK SITE
shall_text: b. Employ the following controls at alternate work sites:

title: ALTERNATE WORK SITE
shall_text: 1. Limit access to the area during CJI processing times to only those personnel authorized by the agency to access or view CJI.

title: ALTERNATE WORK SITE
shall_text: 2. Lock the area, room, or storage container when unattended.

title: ALTERNATE WORK SITE
shall_text: 3. Position information system devices and documents containing CJI in such a way as to prevent unauthorized individuals from access and view.

title: ALTERNATE WORK SITE
shall_text: 4. Follow the encryption requirements found in SC-13 and SC-28 for electronic storage (i.e., data in-transit and data at-rest) of CJI.

title: ALTERNATE WORK SITE
shall_text: c. Assess the effectiveness of controls at alternate work sites; and

title: ALTERNATE WORK SITE
shall_text: d. Provide a means for employees to communicate with information security and privacy personnel in case of incidents.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with planning responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level planning policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the planning policy and the associated planning controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the planning policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current planning:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following; any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: a. Develop security and privacy plans for the system that:

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 1. Are consistent with the organization’s enterprise architecture;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 2. Explicitly define the constituent system components;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 3. Describe the operational context of the system in terms of mission and business processes;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 4. Identify the individuals that fulfill system roles and responsibilities;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 5. Identify the information types processed, stored, and transmitted by the system;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 6. Provide the security categorization of the system, including supporting rationale;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 7. Describe any specific threats to the system that are of concern to the organization;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 8. Provide the results of a privacy risk assessment for systems processing personally identifiable information;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 9. Describe the operational environment for the system and any dependencies on or connections to other systems or system components;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 10. Provide an overview of the security and privacy requirements for the system;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 11. Identify any relevant control baselines or overlays, if applicable;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 12. Describe the controls in place or planned for meeting the security and privacy requirements, including a rationale for any tailoring decisions;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 13. Include risk determinations for security and privacy architecture and design decisions;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 14. Include security- and privacy-related activities affecting the system that require planning and coordination with organizational personnel with system security and privacy planning and plan implementation responsibilities; system developers; organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities; and

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS
shall_text: 15. Are reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to plan implementation.

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS (continued)
shall_text: b. Distribute copies of the plans and communicate subsequent changes to the plans to organizational personnel with system security and privacy planning and plan implementation responsibilities; system developers; organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS (continued)
shall_text: c. Review the system security and privacy plans at least annually or when required due to system changes or modifications;

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS (continued)
shall_text: d. Update the plans to address changes to the system and environment of operation or problems identified during plan implementation or control assessments; and

title: SYSTEM SECURITY AND PRIVACY PLANS (continued)
shall_text: e. Protect the plans from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

title: RULES OF BEHAVIOR
shall_text: a. Establish and provide to individuals requiring access to the system, the rules that describe their responsibilities and expected behavior for information and system usage, security, and privacy;

title: RULES OF BEHAVIOR
shall_text: b. Receive a documented acknowledgment from such individuals, indicating that they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules of behavior, before authorizing access to information and the system;

title: RULES OF BEHAVIOR
shall_text: c. Review and update the rules of behavior at least annually; and

title: RULES OF BEHAVIOR
shall_text: d. Require individuals who have acknowledged a previous version of the rules of behavior to read and re-acknowledge annually, or when the rules are revised or updated.

title: (1) RULES OF BEHAVIOR | SOCIAL MEDIA AND EXTERNAL SITE/APPLICATION USAGE RESTRICTIONS
shall_text: Include in the rules of behavior, restrictions on:

title: (1) RULES OF BEHAVIOR | SOCIAL MEDIA AND EXTERNAL SITE/APPLICATION USAGE RESTRICTIONS
shall_text: (a) Use of social media, social networking sites, and external sites/applications;

title: (1) RULES OF BEHAVIOR | SOCIAL MEDIA AND EXTERNAL SITE/APPLICATION USAGE RESTRICTIONS
shall_text: (b) Posting organizational information on public websites; and

title: (1) RULES OF BEHAVIOR | SOCIAL MEDIA AND EXTERNAL SITE/APPLICATION USAGE RESTRICTIONS
shall_text: (c) Use of organization-provided identifiers (e.g., email addresses) and authentication secrets (e.g., passwords) for creating accounts on external sites/applications.

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY ARCHITECTURES
shall_text: a. Develop security and privacy architectures for the system that:

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY ARCHITECTURES
shall_text: 1. Describe the requirements and approach to be taken for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of organizational information;

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY ARCHITECTURES
shall_text: 2. Describe the requirements and approach to be taken for processing personally identifiable information to minimize privacy risk to individuals;

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY ARCHITECTURES
shall_text: 3. Describe how the architectures are integrated into and support the enterprise architecture; and

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY ARCHITECTURES
shall_text: 4. Describe any assumptions about, and dependencies on, external systems and services;

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY ARCHITECTURES
shall_text: b. Review and update the architectures at least annually or when changes to the system or its environment occur to reflect changes in the enterprise architecture; and

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY ARCHITECTURES
shall_text: c. Reflect planned architecture changes in security and privacy plans, Concept of Operations (CONOPS), criticality analysis, organizational procedures, and procurements and acquisitions.

title: CENTRAL MANAGEMENT
shall_text: The CJISSECPOL is centrally managed by the FBI CJIS ISO.

title: BASELINE SELECTION
shall_text: Select a control baseline for the system.

title: BASELINE TAILORING
shall_text: Tailor the selected control baseline by applying specified tailoring actions.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with personnel security responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level personnel security policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the personnel security policy and the associated personnel security controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the personnel security policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current personnel security:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following assessment or audit findings, security incidents or breaches, or changes in applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following assessment or audit findings, security incidents or breaches, or changes in applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

title: POSITION RISK DESIGNATION
shall_text: a. Assign a risk designation to all organizational positions;

title: POSITION RISK DESIGNATION
shall_text: b. Establish screening criteria for individuals filling those positions; and

title: POSITION RISK DESIGNATION
shall_text: c. Review and update position risk designations as required.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: a. Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to the information system;

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: 1. To properly screen, state of residency and national fingerprint-based record checks shall be conducted. National fingerprint-based record checks must be conducted pursuant to an FBI approved authority such as a federal statute or a state statute approved pursuant to Public Law 92-544. If the person resides in a different state than that of the assigned agency, the agency shall also conduct state (of the agency) record checks. When appropriate, the screening shall be consistent with:

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: a. 5 CFR 731.106; and/or

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: b. Office of Personnel Management policy, regulations, and guidance; and/or

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: c. agency policy, regulations, and guidance.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: Agencies authorized to bypass state repositories in compliance with federal law must only conduct a national fingerprint-based record check.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: Agencies without approved statutory authority authorizing or requiring civil fingerprint-based record checks on personnel with access to CHRI are exempt from this requirement until such time as appropriate statutory authority is obtained to conduct such record checks.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: 2. All requests for access shall be made as specified by the CSO, Authorized Recipient Official, or IA Official. The CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official is authorized to approve access to CJI. All CSO designees shall be from an authorized criminal justice agency. All Authorized Recipient designees shall be employed by the Authorized Recipient Agency.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING
shall_text: 3. If a criminal history record of any kind exists, access to CJI shall not be granted until the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official reviews the matter to determine if access is appropriate.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING (continued)
shall_text: a. If a felony conviction of any kind exists, the agency shall deny access to CJI. However, the requesting agency may ask for a review by the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official in extenuating circumstances where the severity of the offense and the time that has passed would support a possible variance.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING (continued)
shall_text: b. Applicants with a record of misdemeanor offense(s) may be granted access if the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official, determines the nature or severity of the misdemeanor offense(s) do not warrant disqualification. The requesting agency may request the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official review a

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING (continued)
shall_text: dc.e n i a Ilf oaf c arcimceinssa ld heitsetromryi nraetcioornd. of any kind is found on a contractor, the CA shall be formally notified of continuing fitness determination and system access shall be delayed pending review of the criminal history record information. The CA shall in turn notify the contractor’s security officer.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING (continued)
shall_text: 4. If the person appears to be a fugitive or has an arrest history without conviction, the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official shall review the matter to determine if access to CJI is appropriate.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING (continued)
shall_text: 5. If the person already has access to CJI and is subsequently arrested and or convicted, continued access to CJI shall be determined by the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official. This does not implicitly grant hiring/firing authority with the CSA, Authorized Recipient, or IA Official only the authority to grant access to CJI. For offenses other than felonies, the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official has the latitude to delegate continued access determinations.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING (continued)
shall_text: 6. If the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official determines that access to CJI by the person would not be in the public interest, access shall be denied and the person's appointing authority shall be notified in writing of the access denial.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING (continued)
shall_text: 7. The criminal and non-criminal justice agency shall maintain a list of personnel who have been authorized unescorted access to unencrypted CJI and shall, upon request, provide a current copy of the access list to the CSO/designee, Authorized Recipient Official/designee, or IA Official.

title: PERSONNEL SCREENING (continued)
shall_text: b. Recommend rescreening individuals in accordance with PS-3(a)(1) above. The authority authorized for the national fingerprint-based background check must also authorize the rescreening.

title: PERSONNEL TERMINATION
shall_text: Upon termination of individual employment:

title: PERSONNEL TERMINATION
shall_text: a. Disable system access within twenty-four (24) hours;

title: PERSONNEL TERMINATION
shall_text: b. Terminate or revoke any authenticators and credentials associated with the individual;

title: PERSONNEL TERMINATION
shall_text: c. Conduct exit interviews that include a discussion of non-disclosure of CJI and PII;

title: PERSONNEL TERMINATION
shall_text: d. Retrieve all security-related organizational system-related property; and

title: PERSONNEL TERMINATION
shall_text: e. Retain access to organizational information and systems formerly controlled by terminated individual.

title: PERSONNEL TRANSFER
shall_text: a. Review and confirm ongoing operational need for current logical and physical access authorizations to systems and facilities when individuals are reassigned or transferred to other positions within the organization;

title: PERSONNEL TRANSFER
shall_text: b. Initiate appropriate actions such as closing and establishing accounts and changing system access authorizations within twenty-four (24) hours;

title: PERSONNEL TRANSFER
shall_text: c. Modify access authorization as needed to correspond with any changes in operational need due to reassignment or transfer; and

title: PERSONNEL TRANSFER
shall_text: d. Notify organizational personnel with information security responsibilities, organizational personnel with personnel security responsibilities, system/network administrators, and organizational personnel with account management responsibilities prior to personnel transfer.

title: ACCESS AGREEMENTS
shall_text: a. Develop and document access agreements for organizational systems;

title: ACCESS AGREEMENTS
shall_text: b. Review and update the access agreements at least annually; and

title: ACCESS AGREEMENTS
shall_text: c. Verify that individuals requiring access to organizational information and systems:

title: ACCESS AGREEMENTS
shall_text: 1. Sign appropriate access agreements prior to being granted access; and

title: ACCESS AGREEMENTS
shall_text: 2. Re-sign access agreements to maintain access to organizational systems when access agreements have been updated or when signatories change.

title: EXTERNAL PERSONNEL SECURITY
shall_text: a. Establish personnel security requirements, including security roles and responsibilities for external providers;

title: EXTERNAL PERSONNEL SECURITY
shall_text: b. Require external providers to comply with personnel security policies and procedures established by the organization;

title: EXTERNAL PERSONNEL SECURITY
shall_text: c. Document personnel security requirements;

title: EXTERNAL PERSONNEL SECURITY
shall_text: d. Require external providers to notify organizational personnel with information security responsibilities, organizational personnel with personnel security responsibilities, system/network administrators, or organizational personnel with account management responsibilities of any personnel transfers or terminations of external personnel who possess organizational credentials and/or badges, or who have system privileges within twenty-four (24) hours; and

title: EXTERNAL PERSONNEL SECURITY
shall_text: e. Monitor provider compliance with personnel security requirements.

title: PERSONNEL SANCTIONS
shall_text: a. Employ a formal sanctions process for individuals failing to comply with established information security and privacy policies and procedures; and

title: PERSONNEL SANCTIONS
shall_text: b. Notify organizational personnel with information security responsibilities, organizational personnel with personnel security responsibilities, system/network administrators, or organizational personnel with account management responsibilities within twenty-four (24) hours when a formal employee sanctions process is initiated, identifying the individual sanctioned and the reason for the sanction.

title: POSITION DESCRIPTIONS
shall_text: Incorporate security and privacy roles and responsibilities into organizational position descriptions.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with risk assessment responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency Level risk assessment policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the risk assessment policy and the associated risk assessment controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the risk assessment policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current risk assessment:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: SECURITY CATEGORIZATION
shall_text: a. Categorize the system and information it processes, stores, or transmits;

title: SECURITY CATEGORIZATION
shall_text: b. Document the security categorization results, including supporting rationale, in the security plan for the system; and

title: SECURITY CATEGORIZATION
shall_text: c. Verify that the authorizing official or authorizing official designated representative reviews and approves the security categorization decision.

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: a. Conduct a risk assessment, including:

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: 1. Identifying threats to and vulnerabilities in the system;

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: 2. Determining the likelihood and magnitude of harm from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of the system, the information it processes, stores, or transmits, and any related information; and

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: 3. Determining the likelihood and impact of adverse effects on individuals arising from the processing of personally identifiable information;

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: b. Integrate risk assessment results and risk management decisions from the organization and mission or business process perspectives with system-level risk assessments;

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: c. Document risk assessment results in risk assessment report;

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: d. Review risk assessment results at least quarterly;

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: e. Disseminate risk assessment results to organizational personnel with risk assessment responsibilities and organizational personnel with security and privacy responsibilities; and

title: RISK ASSESSMENT
shall_text: f. Update the risk assessment at least quarterly or when there are significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact the security or privacy state of the system.

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING
shall_text: a. Monitor and scan for vulnerabilities in the system and hosted applications at least monthly and when new vulnerabilities potentially affecting the system are identified and reported;

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING
shall_text: b. Employ vulnerability monitoring tools and techniques that facilitate interoperability among tools and automate parts of the vulnerability management process by using standards for:

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING
shall_text: 1. Enumerating platforms, software flaws, and improper configurations;

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING
shall_text: 2. Formatting checklists and test procedures; and

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING
shall_text: 3. Measuring vulnerability impact;

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING (continued)
shall_text: c. Analyze vulnerability scan reports and results from vulnerability monitoring;

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING (continued)
shall_text: d. Remediate legitimate vulnerabilities within the number of days listed;

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING (continued)
shall_text: • Critical–15 days

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING (continued)
shall_text: • High–30 days

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING (continued)
shall_text: • Medium–60 days

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING (continued)
shall_text: • Low–90 days; and

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING (continued)
shall_text: e. Share information obtained from the vulnerability monitoring process and control assessments with organizational personnel with risk assessment, control assessment, and vulnerability scanning responsibilities to help eliminate similar vulnerabilities in other systems; and

title: VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING (continued)
shall_text: f. Employ vulnerability monitoring tools that include the capability to readily update the vulnerabilities to be scanned.

title: (2) VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING | UPDATE VULNERABILITIES TO BE SCANNED
shall_text: Update the system vulnerabilities to be scanned within 24 hours prior to running a new scan or when new vulnerabilities are identified and reported.

title: (5) VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING | PRIVILEGED ACCESS
shall_text: Implement privileged access authorization to information system components containing or processing CJI for vulnerability scanning activities requiring privileged access.

title: (11) VULNERABILITY MONITORING AND SCANNING | PUBLIC DISCLOSURE PROGRAM
shall_text: Establish a public reporting channel for receiving reports of vulnerabilities in organizational systems and system components.

title: RISK RESPONSE
shall_text: Respond to findings from security and privacy assessments, monitoring, and audits in accordance with organizational risk tolerance.

title: CRITICALITY ANALYSIS
shall_text: Identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for information system components containing or processing CJI at the planning, design, development, testing, implementation, and maintenance stages of the system development life cycle.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to: organizational personnel with system and services acquisition responsibilities; organizational personnel with information security and privacy responsibilities; organizational personnel with supply chain risk management responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency/Entity information systems and services acquisition policy for systems that used to process, store, or transmit CJI that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the system and services acquisition policy and the associated system and services acquisition controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities and organizational personnel with system and services acquisition responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the system and services acquisition policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current system and services acquisition:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: ALLOCATION OF RESOURCES
shall_text: a. Determine the high-level information security and privacy requirements for the system or system service in mission and business process planning;

title: ALLOCATION OF RESOURCES
shall_text: b. Determine, document, and allocate the resources required to protect the system or system service as part of the organizational capital planning and investment control process.

title: SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT LIFE CYCLE
shall_text: a. Acquire, develop, and manage the system using an agency documented system development lifecycle process that incorporates information security and privacy considerations;

title: SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT LIFE CYCLE
shall_text: b. Define and document information security and privacy roles and responsibilities throughout the system development life cycle;

title: SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT LIFE CYCLE
shall_text: c. Identify individuals having information security and privacy roles and responsibilities; and

title: SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT LIFE CYCLE
shall_text: d. Integrate the organizational information security and privacy risk management process into system development life cycle activities.

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: Include the following requirements, descriptions, and criteria, explicitly or by reference, using agency defined contract language in the acquisition contract for the system, system component, or system service:

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: a. Security and privacy functional requirements;

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: b. Strength of mechanism requirements;

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: c. Security and privacy assurance requirements;

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: d. Controls needed to satisfy the security and privacy requirements.

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: e. Security and privacy documentation requirements;

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: f. Requirements for protecting security and privacy documentation;

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: g. Description of the system development environment and environment in which the system is intended to operate;

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: h. Allocation of responsibility or identification of parties responsible for information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management; and

title: ACQUISITION PROCESS
shall_text: i. Acceptance criteria.

title: (1) ACQUISITION PROCESS | FUNCTIONAL PROPERTIES OF CONTROLS
shall_text: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to provide a description of the functional properties of the controls to be implemented.

title: (2) ACQUISITION PROCESS | DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION INFORMATION FOR CONTROLS
shall_text: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to provide design and implementation information for the controls that includes: security-relevant external system interfaces; high-level design at and a project plan that addresses sufficient detail to permit analysis and testing of the controls.

title: (9) ACQUISITION PROCESS | FUNCTIONS, PORTS, PROTOCOLS, AND SERVICES IN USE
shall_text: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services intended for organizational use.

title: (10) ACQUISITION PROCESS | USE OF APPROVED PIV PRODUCTS
shall_text: Employ only information technology products on the FIPS 201-approved products list for Personal Identity Verification (PIV) capability implemented within organizational systems.

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: a. Obtain or develop administrator documentation for the system, system component, or system service that describes:

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: 1. Secure configuration, installation, and operation of the system, component, or service;

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: 2. Effective use and maintenance of security and privacy functions and mechanisms; and

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: 3. Known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative or privileged functions;

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: b. Obtain or develop user documentation for the system, system component, or system service that describes:

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: 1. User-accessible security and privacy functions and mechanisms and how to effectively use those functions and mechanisms;

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: 2. Methods for user interaction, which enables individuals to use the system, component, or service in a more secure manner and protect individual privacy; and

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: 3. User responsibilities in maintaining the security of the system, component, or service and privacy of individuals;

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: c. Document steps to obtain system, system component, or system service documentation when such documentation is either unavailable or nonexistent by contacting manufacturers, suppliers, or developers and conducting web-based searches in response; and

title: SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
shall_text: d. Distribute documentation to organizational personnel with system and services responsibilities.

title: SECURITY AND PRIVACY ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
shall_text: Apply agency documented systems security and privacy engineering principles in the specification, design, development, implementation, and modification of the system and system components.

title: (33) SECURITY AND PRIVACY ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES | MINIMIZATION
shall_text: Implement the privacy principle of minimization using only the Personally Identifiable Information necessary to perform system engineering.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES
shall_text: a. Require that providers of external system services comply with organizational security and privacy requirements and employ system and services acquisition security controls in accordance with the CJISSECPOL including the following agreements when applicable:

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES
shall_text: 1. Management control agreement: A NCJA (government) designated to perform criminal justice functions for a CJA shall be eligible for access to the CJI. Access shall be permitted when such designation is authorized pursuant to executive order, statute, regulation, or interagency agreement. The NCJA shall sign and execute a management control agreement (MCA) with the CJA stipulating management control of the criminal justice function remains solely with the CJA. An example of an NCJA (government) is a city information technology (IT) department. An example of an MCA is provided in Appendix

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: 2. Security Addendum: The CJIS Security Addendum is a uniform addendum to an agreement between the government agency and a private contractor, approved by the Director of the FBI, acting for the U.S. Attorney General, as referenced in Title 28 CFR 20.33 (a)(7), which specifically authorizes access to CHRI, limits the use of the information to the purposes for which it is provided, ensures the security and confidentiality of the information is consistent with existing regulations and the CJISSECPOL, provides for sanctions, and contains such other provisions as the Attorney General may require.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: Private contractors designated to:

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: a. Perform criminal justice functions for a CJA; or

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: b. Perform criminal justice dispatching functions or data processing/information services for a NCJA (government), shall be eligible for access to CJI pursuant to an agreement which specifically identifies the private contractor’s purpose and scope of providing services for the administration of criminal justice. The agreement between the CJA/NCJA and the private contractor shall incorporate the CJISSECPOL.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: Private contractors who perform criminal justice functions shall meet the same training and certification criteria required by governmental agencies performing a similar function and shall be subject to the same extent of audit review as are local user agencies. All private contractors who perform criminal justice functions shall acknowledge, via signing of the CJIS Security Addendum Certification page (page H- 8), compliance with all aspects of the CJIS Security Addendum. The CJIS Security Addendum is presented in Appendix H (pages H-6 and 7). Modifications to the CJIS Security Addendum shall be enacted only by the FBI. 3. Outsourcing Standards for Channeling: Channelers designated to request civil fingerprint-based background checks on behalf of a NCJA (public) or NCJA (private) for noncriminal justice functions shall be eligible for access to CJI. Access shall be permitted when such designation is authorized pursuant to federal law or state statute approved by the U.S. Attorney General. All Channelers accessing CJI shall be subject to the terms and conditions described in the Compact Council Security and Management Control Outsourcing Standard. Each Channeler that directly accesses CJI shall also allow the FBI to conduct periodic penetration testing. Channelers leveraging CJI to perform civil functions on behalf of an Authorized Recipient shall meet the same training and certification criteria required by governmental agencies performing a similar function and shall be subject to the same extent of audit review as are local user agencies.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: 4. Outsourcing Standards for Non-Channeling: Contractors designated to perform noncriminal justice ancillary functions on behalf of a NCJA (public) or NCJA (private) for noncriminal justice functions shall be eligible for access to CJI. Access shall be permitted when such designation is authorized pursuant to federal law or state statute approved by the U.S. Attorney General. All contractors accessing CJI shall be subject to the terms and conditions described in the Compact Council Outsourcing Standard for Non-Channelers. Contractors leveraging CJI to perform civil functions on behalf of an Authorized Recipient shall meet the same training and certification criteria required by governmental agencies performing a similar function and shall be subject to the same extent of audit review as are local user agencies.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: b. Define and document organizational oversight and user roles and responsibilities with regard to external system services; and

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: c. Employ the following processes, methods, and techniques to monitor control compliance by external service providers on an ongoing basis:

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: 1. All agencies having access to CJI shall permit an inspection team to conduct an appropriate inquiry and audit of any alleged security violations.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: 2. At a minimum, triennially audit all external service providers which have access to the information system in order to ensure compliance with applicable statutes, regulations, and policies.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: 3. Have the authority to conduct unannounced security inspections and scheduled audits of external service providers facilities.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: 4. Have the authority, on behalf of another CSA, to conduct a CJISSECPOL compliance audit of contractor facilities and provide the results to the requesting CSA. If a subsequent CSA requests an audit of the same contractor facility, the CSA may provide the results of the previous audit unless otherwise notified by the requesting CSA that a new audit be performed.

title: EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: Note: Compliance audit requirements are outlined in the Security and Management Control Outsourcing Standard for Non-Channeling and Channeling related to outsourcing noncriminal justice administrative functions.

title: (2) EXTERNAL SYSTEM SERVICES | IDENTIFICATION OF FUNCTIONS, PORTS, PROTOCOLS, AND SERVICES
shall_text: Require providers of the following external system services to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and other services required for the use of such services: any system with a local, network, or remote connection to an agency information system.

title: DEVELOPER CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT
shall_text: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to:

title: DEVELOPER CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT
shall_text: a. Perform configuration management during system, component, or service during design, development, implementation, operation, and disposal;

title: DEVELOPER CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT
shall_text: b. Document, manage, and control the integrity of changes to security configuration, network diagrams, and system components (hardware, software, firmware) by implementing access restrictions such as least privilege for changes;

title: DEVELOPER CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT
shall_text: c. Implement only organization-approved changes to the system, component, or service;

title: DEVELOPER CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT
shall_text: d. Document approved changes to the system, component, or service and the potential security and privacy impacts of such changes; and

title: DEVELOPER CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT
shall_text: e. Track security flaws and flaw resolution within the system, component, or service and report findings to the individual(s) with information security responsibilities and an individual(s) with system and services acquisition responsibilities.

title: DEVELOPER TESTING AND EVALUATION
shall_text: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service, at all post- design stages of the system development life cycle, to:

title: DEVELOPER TESTING AND EVALUATION
shall_text: a. Develop and implement a plan for ongoing security and privacy control assessments;

title: DEVELOPER TESTING AND EVALUATION
shall_text: b. Perform system and regression testing/evaluation at a level of comprehensive testing;

title: DEVELOPER TESTING AND EVALUATION
shall_text: c. Produce evidence of the execution of the assessment plan and the results of the testing and evaluation;

title: DEVELOPER TESTING AND EVALUATION
shall_text: d. Implement a verifiable flaw remediation process; and

title: DEVELOPER TESTING AND EVALUATION
shall_text: e. Correct flaws identified during testing and evaluation.

title: DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS
shall_text: a. Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to follow a documented development process that:

title: DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS
shall_text: 1. Explicitly addresses security and privacy requirements;

title: DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS
shall_text: 2. Identifies the standards and tools used in the development process;

title: DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS
shall_text: 3. Documents the specific tool options and tool configurations used in the development process; and

title: DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS
shall_text: 4. Documents, manages, and ensures the integrity of changes to the process and/or tools used in development; and

title: DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS
shall_text: b.
