Review the development process, standards, tools, tool options, and tool configurations to determine if the process, standards, tools, tool options and tool configurations selected and employed can satisfy security and privacy requirements during design, development, implementation, operation, and disposal.

title: (1)(3) DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS |CRITICALITY ANALYSIS
shall_text: Require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to perform a criticality analysis:

title: (1)(3) DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS |CRITICALITY ANALYSIS
shall_text: a. At the following decision points in the system development life cycle: design, development, implementation, and operational; and

title: (1)(3) DEVELOPMENT PROCESS, STANDARDS, AND TOOLS |CRITICALITY ANALYSIS
shall_text: b. At the following level of rigor: comprehensive testing.

title: UNSUPPORTED SYSTEM COMPONENTS
shall_text: a. Replace system components when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor, or manufacturer; or

title: UNSUPPORTED SYSTEM COMPONENTS
shall_text: b. Provide the following option for alternative sources for continued support for unsupported components: original manufacturer support, or original contracted vendor support.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with system and communications protection responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level system and communications protection policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the system and communications protection policy and the associated system and communications protection controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with information security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the system and communications protection policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current system and communications protection:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any changes and security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any changes and security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: SEPARATION OF SYSTEM AND USER FUNCTIONALITY
shall_text: Separate user functionality, including user interface services, from system management functionality.

title: INFORMATION IN SHARED SYSTEM RESOURCES
shall_text: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.

title: DENIAL-OF-SERVICE PROTECTION
shall_text: a. Protect against or limit the effects of the following types of denial-of-service events: distributed denial of service, DNS Denial of Service, etc.; and

title: DENIAL-OF-SERVICE PROTECTION
shall_text: b. Employ the following controls to achieve the denial-of-service objective: boundary protection devices and intrusion detection or prevention devices.

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION
shall_text: a. Monitor and control communications at the external managed interfaces to the system and at key internal managed interfaces within the system;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION
shall_text: b. Implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal organizational networks; and

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION
shall_text: c. Connect to external networks or systems only through managed interfaces consisting of boundary protection devices arranged in accordance with an organizational security and privacy architecture.

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | ACCESS POINTS
shall_text: Limit the number of external network connections to the system.

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | EXTERNAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES
shall_text: (a) Implement a managed interface for each external telecommunication service;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | EXTERNAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES
shall_text: (b) Establish a traffic flow policy for each managed interface;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | EXTERNAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES
shall_text: (c) Protect the confidentiality and integrity of the information being transmitted across each interface;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | EXTERNAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES
shall_text: (d) Document each exception to the traffic flow policy with a supporting mission or business need and duration of that need;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | EXTERNAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: (e) Review exceptions to the traffic flow policy annually, after any incident, and after any major changes impacting the information system, while remove exceptions that are no longer supported by an explicit mission or business need;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | EXTERNAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: (f) Prevent unauthorized exchange of control plane traffic with external networks;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | EXTERNAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: (g) Publish information to enable remote networks to detect unauthorized control plane traffic from internal networks; and

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | EXTERNAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS SERVICES (continued)
shall_text: (h) Filter unauthorized control plane traffic from external networks.

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | DENY BY DEFAULT — ALLOW BY EXCEPTION
shall_text: Deny network communications traffic by default and allow network communications traffic by exception at boundary devices for information systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | SPLIT TUNNELING FOR REMOTE DEVICES
shall_text: Prevent split tunneling for remote devices connecting to organizational systems.

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | ROUTE TRAFFIC TO AUTHENTICATED PROXY SERVERS
shall_text: Route all internal communications traffic that may be proxied, except traffic specifically exempted by organizational personnel with information security responsibilities, to all untrusted networks through authenticated proxy servers at managed interfaces.

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION
shall_text: For systems that process personally identifiable information:

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION
shall_text: (a) Apply the following processing rules to data elements of personally identifiable information: all applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION
shall_text: (b) Monitor for permitted processing at the external interfaces to the system and at key internal boundaries within the system;

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION
shall_text: (c) Document each processing exception; and

title: BOUNDARY PROTECTION | PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION
shall_text: (d) Review and remove exceptions that are no longer supported.

title: TRANSMISSION CONFIDENTIALITY AND INTEGRITY
shall_text: Protect the confidentiality and integrity of transmitted information.

title: TRANSMISSION CONFIDENTIALITY AND INTEGRITY
shall_text: Metadata derived from unencrypted CJI shall be protected in the same manner as CJI and shall not be used for any advertising or other commercial purposes by any cloud service provider or other associated entity.

title: TRANSMISSION CONFIDENTIALITY AND INTEGRITY | CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROTECTION
shall_text: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and detect unauthorized changes or access to CJI during transmission.

title: NETWORK DISCONNECT
shall_text: Terminate the network connection associated with a communications session at the end of the session or after one (1) hour of inactivity.

title: NETWORK DISCONNECT
shall_text: NOTE: In the interest of safety, devices that are: (1) part of a criminal justice conveyance; or (2) used to perform dispatch functions and located within a physically secure location; or (3) terminals designated solely for the purpose of receiving alert notifications (i.e., receive only terminals or ROT) and used within physically secure location facilities that remain staffed when in operation, are exempt from this requirement.

title: CRYPTOGRAPHIC KEY ESTABLISHMENT AND MANAGEMENT
shall_text: Establish and manage cryptographic keys when cryptography is employed within the system in accordance with the following key management requirements: encryption key generation, distribution, storage, access, and destruction is controlled by the agency.

title: CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROTECTION
shall_text: a. Determine the use of encryption for CJI in-transit when outside a physically secure location; and

title: CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROTECTION
shall_text: b. Implement the following types of cryptography required for each specified cryptographic use: cryptographic modules which are Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 140-3 certified, or a FIPS validated algorithm for symmetric key encryption and decryption (FIPS 197 [AES]), with a symmetric cipher key of at least 256-bit strength for CJI in-transit.

title: CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROTECTION
shall_text: NOTE: Subsequent versions of approved cryptographic modules that are under current review for FIPS 140-3 compliancy can be used in the interim until certification is complete. FIPS 140-2 certificates will not be acceptable after September 21, 2026.

title: COLLABORATIVE COMPUTING DEVICES AND APPLICATIONS
shall_text: a. Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and applications; and

title: COLLABORATIVE COMPUTING DEVICES AND APPLICATIONS
shall_text: b. Provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.

title: PUBLIC KEY INFRASTRUCTURE CERTIFICATES
shall_text: a. Issue public key certificates under an agency-level certificate authority or obtain public key certificates from an approved service provider; and

title: PUBLIC KEY INFRASTRUCTURE CERTIFICATES
shall_text: b. Include only approved trust anchors in trust stores or certificate stores managed by the organization.

title: MOBILE CODE
shall_text: a. Define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies; and

title: MOBILE CODE
shall_text: b. Authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code within the system.

title: SECURE NAME/ADDRESS RESOLUTION SERVICE (AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE)
shall_text: a. Provide additional data origin authentication and integrity verification artifacts along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns in response to external name/address resolution queries; and

title: SECURE NAME/ADDRESS RESOLUTION SERVICE (AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE)
shall_text: b. Provide the means to indicate the security status of child zones and (if the child supports secure resolution services) to enable verification of a chain of trust among parent and child domains, when operating as part of a distributed, hierarchical namespace.

title: SECURE NAME/ADDRESS RESOLUTION SERVICE (RECURSIVE OR CACHING RESOLVER)
shall_text: Request and perform data origin authentication and data integrity verification on the name/address resolution responses the system receives from authoritative sources.

title: ARCHITECTURE AND PROVISIONING FOR NAME/ADDRESS RESOLUTION SERVICE
shall_text: Ensure the systems that collectively provide name/address resolution service for an organization are fault-tolerant and implement internal and external role separation.

title: SESSION AUTHENTICITY
shall_text: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.

title: PROTECTION OF INFORMATION AT REST
shall_text: Protect the confidentiality and integrity of the following information at rest: CJI when outside physically secure locations using cryptographic modules which are certified FIPS 140-3 with a symmetric cipher key of at least 256-bit strength, or FIPS 197 with a symmetric cipher key of at least 256-bit strength.

title: PROTECTION OF INFORMATION AT REST
shall_text: Metadata derived from unencrypted CJI shall be protected in the same manner as CJI and shall not be used for any advertising or other commercial purposes by any cloud service provider or other associated entity.

title: PROTECTION OF INFORMATION AT REST
shall_text: The storage of CJI, regardless of encryption status, shall only be permitted in cloud environments (e.g., government or third-party/commercial datacenters, etc.) which reside within the physical boundaries of APB-member country (i.e., United States, U.S. territories, Indian Tribes, and Canada) and are under legal authority of an APB-member agency (i.e., United States–federal/state/territory, Indian Tribe, or the Royal Canadian Mounted Police).

title: PROTECTION OF INFORMATION AT REST
shall_text: Note: This restriction does not apply to exchanges of CJI with foreign government agencies under international exchange agreements (e.g., the Preventing and Combating Serious Crime agreements, fugitive extracts, and exchanges made for humanitarian and criminal investigatory purposes in particular circumstances).

title: PROTECTION OF INFORMATION AT REST | CRYPTOGRAPHIC PROTECTION
shall_text: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of the following information at rest on information systems and digital media outside physically secure locations: CJI.

title: PROCESS ISOLATION
shall_text: Maintain a separate execution domain for each executing system process.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to all organizational personnel with system and information integrity responsibilities and information system owners:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level system and information integrity policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (a) Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: (b) Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the system and information integrity policy and the associated system and information integrity controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate organizational personnel with system and information integrity responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the system and information integrity policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current system and information integrity:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: FLAW REMEDIATION
shall_text: a. Identify, report, and correct system flaws;

title: FLAW REMEDIATION
shall_text: b. Test software and firmware updates related to flaw remediation for effectiveness and potential side effects before installation;

title: FLAW REMEDIATION
shall_text: c. Install security-relevant software and firmware updates within the number of days listed after the release of the updates;

title: FLAW REMEDIATION
shall_text: • Critical – 15 days

title: FLAW REMEDIATION
shall_text: • High – 30 days

title: FLAW REMEDIATION
shall_text: • Medium – 60 days

title: FLAW REMEDIATION
shall_text: • Low – 90 days; and

title: FLAW REMEDIATION
shall_text: d. Incorporate flaw remediation into the organizational configuration management process.

title: (2) FLAW REMEDIATION | AUTOMATED FLAW REMEDIATION STATUS
shall_text: Determine if system components have applicable security-relevant software and firmware updates installed using vulnerability scanning tools as least monthly or following any security incidents involving CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: MALICIOUS CODE PROTECTION
shall_text: a. Implement signature-based and/or nonsignature-based malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code;

title: MALICIOUS CODE PROTECTION
shall_text: b. Automatically update malicious code protection mechanisms as new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures;

title: MALICIOUS CODE PROTECTION
shall_text: c. Configure malicious code protection mechanisms to:

title: MALICIOUS CODE PROTECTION
shall_text: 1. Perform periodic scans of the system at least daily and real-time scans of files from external sources at network entry and exit points and on all servers and endpoint devices as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed in accordance with organizational policy; and

title: MALICIOUS CODE PROTECTION (continued)
shall_text: 2. Block or quarantine malicious code, take mitigating action(s), and when necessary, implement incident response procedures; and send alert to system/network administrators and/or organizational personnel with information security responsibilities in response to malicious code detection; and

title: MALICIOUS CODE PROTECTION (continued)
shall_text: d. Address the receipt of false positives during malicious code detection and eradication and the resulting potential impact on the availability of the system.

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: a. Monitor the system to detect:

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: 1. Attacks and indicators of potential attacks in accordance with the following monitoring objectives:

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: a. Intrusion detection and prevention

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: b. Malicious code protection

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: c. Vulnerability scanning

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: d. Audit record monitoring

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: e. Network monitoring

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: f. Firewall monitoring;

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: 2. Unauthorized local, network, and remote connections;

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: b. Identify unauthorized use of the system through the following techniques and methods: event logging (ref. Audit and Accountability (AU));

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: c. Invoke internal monitoring capabilities or deploy monitoring devices:

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: 1. Strategically within the system to collect organization-determined essential information; and

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: 2. At ad hoc locations within the system to track specific types of transactions of interest to the organization;

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: d. Analyze detected events and anomalies;

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: e. Adjust the level of system monitoring activity when there is a change in risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation;

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: f. Obtain legal opinion regarding system monitoring activities; and

title: SYSTEM MONITORING
shall_text: g. Provide intrusion detection and prevention systems, malicious code protection software, scanning tools, audit record monitoring software, network monitoring, and firewall monitoring software logs to organizational personnel with information security responsibilities weekly.

title: (2) SYSTEM MONITORING | AUTOMATED TOOLS AND MECHANISMS FOR REAL-TIME ANALYSIS
shall_text: Employ automated tools and mechanisms to support near-real-time analysis of events.

title: (4) SYSTEM MONITORING | INBOUND AND OUTBOUND COMMUNICATIONS TRAFFIC
shall_text: a. Determine criteria for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions for inbound and outbound communications traffic;

title: (4) SYSTEM MONITORING | INBOUND AND OUTBOUND COMMUNICATIONS TRAFFIC
shall_text: b. Monitor inbound and outbound communications traffic continuously for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions such as: the presence of malicious code or unauthorized use of legitimate code or credentials within organizational systems or propagating among system components, signaling to external systems, and the unauthorized exporting of information.

title: (5) SYSTEM MONITORING | SYSTEM- GENERATED ALERTS
shall_text: Alert organizational personnel with system monitoring responsibilities when the following system-generated indications of compromise or potential compromise occur: inappropriate or unusual activities with security or privacy implications.

title: SECURITY ALERTS, ADVISORIES, AND DIRECTIVES
shall_text: a. Receive system security alerts, advisories, and directives from external source(s) (e.g., CISA, Multi-State Information Sharing & Analysis Center [MS-ISAC], U.S. Computer Emergency Readiness Team [USCERT], hardware/software providers, federal/state advisories, etc.) on an ongoing basis;

title: SECURITY ALERTS, ADVISORIES, AND DIRECTIVES
shall_text: b. Generate internal security alerts, advisories, and directives as deemed necessary;

title: SECURITY ALERTS, ADVISORIES, AND DIRECTIVES
shall_text: c. Issue security alerts, advisories, and directives to: organizational personnel implementing, operating, maintaining, and using the system; and

title: SECURITY ALERTS, ADVISORIES, AND DIRECTIVES
shall_text: d. Implement security directives in accordance with established time frames, or notify the issuing organization of the degree of noncompliance.

title: SOFTWARE, FIRMWARE, AND INFORMATION INTEGRITY
shall_text: a. Employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to software, firmware, and information systems that contain or process CJI; and

title: SOFTWARE, FIRMWARE, AND INFORMATION INTEGRITY
shall_text: b. Take the following actions when unauthorized changes to the software, firmware, and information are detected: notify organizational personnel responsible for software, firmware, and/or information integrity and implement incident response procedures as appropriate.

title: (1) SOFTWARE, FIRMWARE, AND INFORMATION INTEGRITY | INTEGRITY CHECKS
shall_text: Perform an integrity check of software, firmware, and information systems that contain or process CJI at agency-defined transitional states or security relevant events at least weekly or in an automated fashion.

title: (7) SOFTWARE, FIRMWARE, AND INFORMATION INTEGRITY | INTEGRATION OF DETECTION AND RESPONSE
shall_text: Incorporate the detection of the following unauthorized changes into the organizational incident response capability: unauthorized changes to established configuration setting or the unauthorized elevation of system privileges.

title: SPAM PROTECTION
shall_text: a. Employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry points to detect and act on unsolicited messages; and

title: SPAM PROTECTION
shall_text: b. Update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available in accordance with organizational configuration management policy and procedures.

title: (2) SPAM PROTECTION | AUTOMATIC UPDATES
shall_text: Automatically update spam protection mechanisms at least daily.

title: INFORMATION INPUT VALIDATION
shall_text: Check the validity of the following information inputs: all inputs to web/application servers, database servers, and any system or application input that might receive or process CJI.

title: ERROR HANDLING
shall_text: a. Generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited; and

title: ERROR HANDLING
shall_text: b. Reveal error messages only to organizational personnel with information security responsibilities.

title: INFORMATION MANAGEMENT AND RETENTION
shall_text: Manage and retain information within the system and information output from the system in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, guidelines and operational requirements.

title: (1) INFORMATION MANAGEMENT AND RETENTION | LIMIT PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION ELEMENTS
shall_text: Limit personally identifiable information being processed in the information life cycle to the minimum PII necessary to achieve the purpose for which it is collected (see Section 4.3).

title: (2) INFORMATION MANAGEMENT AND RETENTION | MINIMIZE PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION IN TESTING, TRAINING, AND RESEARCH
shall_text: Use the following techniques to minimize the use of personally identifiable information for research, testing, or training: data obfuscation, randomization, anonymization, or use of synthetic data.

title: (3) INFORMATION MANAGEMENT AND RETENTION | INFORMATION DISPOSAL
shall_text: Use the following techniques to dispose of, destroy, or erase information following the retention period: as defined in MP-6.

title: MEMORY PROTECTION
shall_text: Implement the following controls to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution: data execution prevention and address space layout randomization.

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Develop, document, and disseminate to organizational personnel with supply chain risk management responsibilities:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Agency-level supply chain risk management policy that:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: a. Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures to facilitate the implementation of the supply chain risk management policy and the associated supply chain risk management controls;

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: b. Designate an organizational personnel with security responsibilities to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the supply chain risk management policy and procedures; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: c. Review and update the current supply chain risk management:

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 1. Policy annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI; and

title: POLICY AND PROCEDURES
shall_text: 2. Procedures annually and following any security incidents involving unauthorized access to CJI or systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: SUPPLY CHAIN RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: a. Develop a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with the research and development, design, manufacturing, acquisition, delivery, integration, operations and maintenance, and disposal of the following systems, system components or system services: systems used to process, store, or transmit CJI;

title: SUPPLY CHAIN RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: b. Review and update the supply chain risk management plan annually or as required, to address threat, organizational or environmental changes; and

title: SUPPLY CHAIN RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN
shall_text: c. Protect the supply chain risk management plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

title: (1) SUPPLY CHAIN RISK MANAGEMENT PLAN | ESTABLISH SCRM TEAM
shall_text: Establish a supply chain risk management team consisting of individuals with security responsibilities and supply chain risk management responsibilities to lead and support the following SCRM activities: information technology, contracting, information security, privacy, mission or business, legal, supply chain and logistics, acquisition, business continuity, and other relevant functions.

title: ACQUISITION STRATEGIES, TOOLS, AND METHODS
shall_text: Employ the following acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks: use preferred suppliers who can provide attestation or demonstration of compliance with state or federal standards.

title: NOTIFICATION AGREEMENTS
shall_text: Establish agreements and procedures with entities involved in the supply chain for the system, system component, or system service for the notification of supply chain compromises to systems used to access, process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: INSPECTION OF SYSTEMS OR COMPONENTS
shall_text: Inspect the following systems or system components upon initial procurement and periodically as needed to detect tampering: systems used to access, process, store, or transmit CJI.

title: COMPONENT DISPOSAL
shall_text: Dispose of CJI using the techniques and methods as described in Media Protection (MP).

title: Cellular Service Abroad
shall_text: When devices are authorized to access CJI outside the U.S., agencies shall perform an inspection to ensure that all controls are in place and functioning properly in accordance with the agency's policies prior to and after deployment outside of the U.S.

title: Bluetooth
shall_text: Organizational security policy shall be used to dictate the use of Bluetooth and its associated devices based on the agency's operational and business processes.

title: Mobile Hotspots
shall_text: When an agency allows mobile devices that are approved to access or store CJI to function as a Wi-Fi hotspot connecting to the Internet, they shall be configured:

title: Mobile Hotspots
shall_text: 1. Enable encryption on the hotspot

title: Mobile Hotspots
shall_text: 2. Change the hotspot's default SSID

title: Mobile Hotspots
shall_text: a. Ensure the hotspot SSID does not identify the device make/model or agency ownership

title: Mobile Hotspots
shall_text: 3. Create a wireless network password (Pre-shared key)

title: Mobile Hotspots
shall_text: 4. Enable the hotspot’s port filtering/blocking features if present

title: Mobile Hotspots
shall_text: 5. Only allow connections from agency controlled devices

title: Mobile Hotspots
shall_text: OR 1. Have a MDM solution to provide the same security as identified in 1 - 5 above.

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: Devices that have had any unauthorized changes made to them (including but not limited to being rooted or jailbroken) shall not be used to process, store, or transmit CJI at any time.

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: User agencies shall implement the following controls when directly accessing CJI from devices running limited feature operating system:

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: 1. Ensure that CJI is only transferred between CJI authorized applications and storage areas of the device.

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: 2. MDM with centralized administration configured and implemented to perform at least the following controls:

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: a. Remote locking of the device

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: b. Remote wiping of the device

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: c. Setting and locking device configuration

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: d. Detection of "rooted" and "jailbroken" devices

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: e. Enforcement of folder or disk level encryption

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: f. Application of mandatory policy settings on the device

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: g. Detection of unauthorized configurations

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: h. Detection of unauthorized software or applications

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: i. Ability to determine location of agency controlled devices

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: j. Prevention of unpatched devices from accessing CJI or CJI systems

title: Mobile Device Management (MDM)
shall_text: k. Automatic device wiping after a specified number of failed access attempts

title: Patching/Updates
shall_text: Agencies shall monitor mobile devices to ensure their patch and update state is current.

title: Malicious Code Protection
shall_text: Agencies that allow smartphones and tablets to access CJI shall have a process to approve the use of specific software or applications on the devices.

title: Personal Firewall
shall_text: A personal firewall shall be employed on all devices that have a full-feature operating system (i.e. laptops or tablets with Windows or Linux/Unix operating systems).

title: Personal Firewall
shall_text: At a minimum, the personal firewall shall perform the following activities:

title: Personal Firewall
shall_text: 1. Manage program access to the Internet.

title: Personal Firewall
shall_text: 2. Block unsolicited requests to connect to the PC.

title: Personal Firewall
shall_text: 3. Filter Incoming traffic by IP address or protocol.

title: Personal Firewall
shall_text: 4. Filter Incoming traffic by destination ports.

title: Personal Firewall
shall_text: 5. Maintain an IP traffic log.

title: Incident Response
shall_text: In addition to the requirements in Section 5.3 Incident Response, agencies shall develop additional or enhanced incident reporting and handling procedures to address mobile device operating scenarios.

title: Incident Response
shall_text: Special reporting procedures for mobile devices shall apply in any of the following situations:

title: Incident Response
shall_text: 1. Loss of device control. For example:

title: Incident Response
shall_text: a. Device known to be locked, minimal duration of loss

title: Incident Response
shall_text: b. Device lock state unknown, minimal duration of loss

title: Incident Response
shall_text: c. Device lock state unknown, extended duration of loss

title: Incident Response
shall_text: d. Device known to be unlocked, more than momentary duration of loss

title: Incident Response
shall_text: 2. Total loss of device

title: Incident Response
shall_text: 3. Device compromise

title: Incident Response
shall_text: 4. Device loss or compromise outside the United States

title: Access Control
shall_text: Accesscontrol (see AccessControl (AC)) shall be accomplished bythe application that accesses CJI.

title: Local Device Authentication
shall_text: When mobile devices are authorized for use in accessing CJI, local device authentication shall be used to unlock the device for use.

title: Local Device Authentication
shall_text: The authenticator used shall meet the requirements in Identification and Authentication (IA).

title: Advanced Authentication
shall_text: WhenaccessingCJIfromanauthorizedmobiledevice,advancedauthenticationshallbe used by the authorized user unless the access to CJI is indirect as described in Identification and Authentication (IA). If access in indirect, then AA is not required.

title: Compensating Controls
shall_text: Before CSOs consider approval of compensating controls, Mobile Device Management (MDM) shall be implemented per Section 5.20.2.

title: Compensating Controls
shall_text: The compensating controls shall:

title: Compensating Controls
shall_text: 1. Meet the intent of the CJIS Security Policy AA requirement

title: Compensating Controls
shall_text: 2. Provide a similar level of protection or security as the original AA requirement

title: Compensating Controls
shall_text: 3. Not rely upon the existing requirements for AA as compensating controls

title: Compensating Controls
shall_text: 4. Expire upon the CSO approved date or when a compliant AA solution is implemented.

title: Compensating Controls

shall_text: Possessionandregistrationofanagency-issuedsmartphoneortabletasanindicationitis the authorized user

shall_text: Use of device certificates as per Section 5.20.7.3 Device Certificates

title: Compensating Controls
shall_text: Implemented CJIS Security Policy compliant standard authenticator protection on the secure location where CJI is stored

title: Device Certificates
shall_text: When certificates or cryptographic keys used to authenticate a mobile device are used in lieu of compensating controls for advanced authentication, they shall be:

title: Device Certificates
shall_text: 1. Protected against being extracted from the device

title: Device Certificates
shall_text: 2. Configured for remote wipe on demand or self-deletion based on a number of unsuccessful login or access attempts

title: Device Certificates
shall_text: 3. Configured to use a secure authenticator (i.e. password, PIN) to unlock the key for use
